Emotions and appraisals — the thinnest slice in the repo, by commitment.

DOCTRINE. * THIN MEANS THIN (Principle 15 discipline): this slice ships the minimum its named consumers require and STOPS. Growth requires a new consumer, not modeling pleasure; docs.md records the size budget and what demand would justify expansion (a sensory-environment or narrative consumer). * An Emotion is an intrinsic mode inhering in one agent (the Desire/Intention pattern, #350). Episodic scope rides validFrom/validUntil on the statement — NO tenure class here (thin means thin); promote to the StandpointTenure idiom only if a consumer ever demands it. * EmotionType is an OPEN vocabulary seeded from the EmotionML standard sets (Plutchik's primary eight); registry-independent, contestable, never a tree (the Genre/Register precedent). * APPRAISALS ARE OBSERVATIONS: dimensional readings (PAD: valence, arousal, dominance) and qualitative aesthetic judgements (elegance, sublimity, kitsch — open) are vantage-indexed cells. Two critics disagreeing are two cells (Principle 9). Attributed emotion vs self-report is the vantage axis too: self-report is top authority for the subject's own standpoint (the facetVantage precedent) — docs, no new machinery. * ALIGNMENTS DEFERRED to the compiler-arc window: MFOEM (linkage-only, BFO lineage), EmotionML vocabularies, WordNet-Affect; W3C EmotionML projection with declared loss (vantage collapses to EmotionML's single-annotator model — flagged). Target list fixed in #356.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/affect

docs.title: GMEOW Agentic Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Agentic Module — tool-call provenance: an agent's ACTIONS join the same provenance graph as its claims (issue #390). DELIBERATELY THIN.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/agentic CURIE: gmeow:slices/agentic

Type: owl:Ontology

Agentic tool-call provenance — the ModelInvocation idiom one level down.

DOCTRINE. * THE MODELINVOCATION IDIOM, EXACTLY (#390): ToolCall is a gufo:EventType under gmeow:Activity with one functional agent link (usedTool, mirroring usedModel) and verbatim call parameters as datatype properties (mirroring the sampling trio). 'Which tool, called by which invocation, with what arguments, at what time?' is answerable after the fact. * NO FORWARD OUTPUT ENTITY PROPERTY (Principle 5): an entity the call produced — a stored claim, a written file, a minted node — links BACK via gmeow:wasGeneratedBy, exactly as claims link back to their ModelInvocation. gmeow:toolResult records the verbatim PAYLOAD of the event itself, never an entity link. * VERBATIM-OR-DIGEST: toolArguments/toolResult carry the byte-faithful payload. For large payloads store a content digest literal instead ("blake3:…" — the gmeow:contentDigest convention from the sources slice): the digest IS the value, resolvable from a content-addressed store. Self-describing prefixes keep the two forms distinguishable. * TOOLS ARE SOFTWARE AGENTS — deliberately no Tool subclass: tool-ness is the role the agent plays in this call event, not an identity (roles classify, never reify — the Persona lesson, #355). An MCP tool, a search service, and a code runner are SoftwareAgents that happen to be called. * calledByInvocation IS OPTIONAL: a recording harness may not expose the requesting model invocation; a ToolCall without one is still auditable provenance. The result feeds a LATER invocation — that ordering is temporal (atTime), not a TBox link. * THIN MEANS THIN (Principle 15): the named consumer is Project Lillith's agentic mode; the gmeow memory MCP triad is the first live producer (its store/revise calls record themselves). Five terms; growth requires a new consumer — trajectory aggregates (runs, episodes, plans) wait for one. * ALIGNMENTS: ToolCall is prov:Activity by inheritance (the provenance set). OpenAI function-calling, Anthropic tool_use, and MCP tool schemas are JSON specs with no stable RDF namespace — bridging is a projection concern (#58, the OpenLineage precedent), recorded in the mapping trailer.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/agentic

docs.title: GMEOW Spatial Aggregation Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Spatial Aggregation Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/aggregation CURIE: gmeow:slices/aggregation

Type: owl:Ontology

Spatial aggregation and statistical summarisation over places — count, sum, average, density, centroid, and binning. Realises the #42 Location-as-reference-frame epic and the #101 cross-cutting aggregation concern.

Every aggregation is a gmeow:Measurement (the universal observation stack), so vantage, observedFeature, observationResult, confidence, granularity, and temporal scope are inherited without duplication (Principle 4). The aggregation region is the observedFeature; the result is a gmeow:ScalarQuantity. The actual arithmetic — counting, density computation, centroid calculation, binning — is performed by the solver layer (Principle 12), never materialised as asserted triples in the OWL core.

Privacy (k-anonymity, coarsening, suppression) is handled by the existing projection layer: gmeow:coarsenTo, gmeow:displayable false, and gmeow:hasSensitivity govern whether and at what granularity an aggregation result may be published (Principle 10). K-anonymity thresholds ("publish only if count >= K") remain a solver-layer computation (Principle 12).

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/aggregation

docs.title: GMEOW AI Claim Module
docs.text:
The AI claim layer (#54), built the constitutional way: GMEOW already IS a claim model. The unified observation stance (CONSTITUTION P9) makes gmeow:Observation the universal claim construct — an LLM output is a StandpointClaim whose vantage is the model agent, its epistemics (confidence, accordingTo, the clocks) ride RDF 1.2 statement annotations, its verdicts ride the standpoint modalities (including gmeow:bullshit) and the deception slice's veridicality, and its evaluation is the norms extension's judge-as-vantage Assessment. This module therefore mints ONLY what is genuinely absent: the retrieval segment (Chunk) and its evidence seam, the prompt artifact, the model-invocation activity, the model card, the surfaced Contradiction, and the memory role. Everything else is doctrine over existing terms — see docs.md, the slice's real deliverable.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/ai CURIE: gmeow:slices/ai

Type: owl:Ontology

A GeneratedClaim is a QUERY, not a class: a StandpointClaim whose vantage is a SoftwareAgent and which gmeow:wasGeneratedBy a ModelInvocation — a direct triple on the claim individual; on the reified RDF 1.2 statement form the invocation link is gmeow:mappedFrom, keeping axiom annotations AnnotationProperty-clean for the DL downcast (P3). A hallucination is a claim node with no gmeow:groundedIn span — flagged (P10), never deleted. Pipeline observability (corpus, embeddings, indexes, retrievals, GraphRAG artifacts) lives in extensions/graphrag, consumer-named per P15.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/ai

Reuses the universal Observation stack, TemporalMeasurement, Place, Event, and the lexicon/attestation layer. Defers general archaeological domain modeling to #129.

docs.title: GMEOW Attestation Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Attestation Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/attestation CURIE: gmeow:slices/attestation

Type: owl:Ontology

Cross-cutting certified attestation layer: signed claims, signed artifacts, verification results, transparency-log evidence, and ledger/blockchain evidence. Separates the claim/observation (what is asserted) from the attestation (who vouches for it under which policy) from the cryptographic evidence (signature) from the verification result (an observed outcome, not truth itself). Aligns to PROV-O, in-toto, SLSA, DSSE, Sigstore, Rekor, SCITT, W3C Verifiable Credentials, C2PA, RATS/EAT, and nanopublications by reference (Principle 5).

MODEL BOUNDARIES (Principles 1, 9, 12). - A valid signature proves integrity and signer key control, NOT truth. - A certification/attestation proves an issuer made a statement under a policy, NOT that the statement is globally correct. - A transparency log proves inclusion, NOT correctness. - Blockchain inclusion proves ledger inclusion under chain rules, NOT real-world truth. - Cryptographic verification, policy evaluation, chain-finality checks, and quality scoring live in the solver layer, not the reasoner.

REUSE. - Statement-level metadata (confidence, standpoint, temporal scope) reuses the cross-cutting annotation properties (provenance, standpoint, temporal modules). - Content identity reuses gmeow:contentDigest and gmeow:versionFingerprint. - The universal claim stack (Observation) is the target of attestedClaim, NOT the parent of Attestation.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/attestation

docs.title: GMEOW Calendar and Scheduling Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Calendar and Scheduling Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/calendar CURIE: gmeow:slices/calendar

Type: owl:Ontology

The calendar and scheduling slice: recurrence, availability, RSVP, reminders, tasks, and time zones on top of events. Builds on the events module (#41) and temporal module, reusing Event, Participation, EventSeries/RecurrenceRule, TimeInterval, and the four clocks. Aligns to iCalendar RFC 5545/5546/6047/4791/6638/7809, jCal RFC 7265, xCal RFC 6321, schema.org Schedule/EventSeries, OWL-Time, and Wikidata by reference.

DESIGN PRINCIPLES. * Schedule ≠ occurrence: an EventSchedule (rule + anchor + time zone) GENERATES Event occurrences; it is not itself the occurrence (Principle 1). * Reify social acts as relators: EventInvitation and Availability use the Participation idiom — never flat properties. * Open value vocabularies, not subclasses: invitationStatus, rsvpStatus, availabilityStatus, reminderAction, taskStatus, exceptionType are individuals, never Event/Task subclasses (Principle 9). * Cancelled ≠ deleted (Principle 10): a cancelled/rescheduled occurrence is displayable false + a ScheduleException, retained, never erased. * Contested times coexist (#43): disputed times are standpoint-indexed via accordingTo; no single winner. * DL-clean time: datetimes are xsd:dateTime, durations xsd:duration; recurrence as a literal rule (RFC 5545 text) + structured form, kept out of OWL cardinality.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/calendar

docs.title: GMEOW Creative Works Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Creative Works Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/creative-works CURIE: gmeow:slices/creative-works

Type: owl:Ontology

The WEMI spine for creative and intellectual works — Work, Expression, Manifestation, Item — reconstructed from native GMEOW primitives (frame-relativity, reified events, relators, standpoints) and bridged to FRBR/LRMoo/CIDOC/schema.org by reference (Principle 5), never by axiom import.

DOCTRINE. * The four tiers are gufo:Kinds with distinct identity criteria (Work=abstract content, Expression=language/notation frame, Manifestation=edition/format, Item=single copy); CreativeWork is the gufo:Category umbrella over them. * Expression variance is carried by gmeow:hasReferenceFrame (language, script, notation, arrangement) — never a subclass taxonomy (Principle 9). * Creation is a reified gmeow:Event with an eventType value — no Event subclasses (Principle 12). * Contribution is a reified gmeow:Relator with flat shortcuts for the 80% case (flat-first, reify-on-demand). * Format, role, genre, and medium are open value vocabularies (individuals), never subclasses (Principle 9). * No primary/privileged title or edition (Principle 9); suppressed titles and withdrawn standpoints use gmeow:displayable false (Principle 10). * Complex lineage (translations-as-versions, collected volumes, withdrawn releases) reuses the generic VersionSet / VersionMembership machinery (#161).

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/creative-works

docs.title: GMEOW Deception Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Deception Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/deception CURIE: gmeow:slices/deception

Type: owl:Ontology

Cross-cutting deception, falsehood, and misinformation facility. Builds on the standpoint module (#43) and the event module (#41) to model deceptive acts as standpoint-indexed divergences between what a party holds true and what they project. Part of the Deception EPIC (#212).

DOCTRINE. * No isFalse / isDeceptive axiom and no boolean truth datatype property (Principles 1, 12). A falsehood is a frame-relative gmeow:StandpointClaim whose claimModality = gmeow:refuted (settled-false per a designated reference frame). Deceptiveness is asserted as a standpoint-indexed, attributed, confidence-weighted claim that coexists with its denial (Principle 9). * A deception is the divergence held-standpoint ≠ projected-standpoint, both modelled as ordinary StandpointClaims; the gap is the act, not a truth verdict. * Deception kind is an open gmeow:eventType value, never a subclass (events.ttl doctrine). * Intent is kept OUT of the logic: gmeow:deceptiveIntentClaim is a StandpointClaim (attributed/defeasible — vantage = assessor, wasAttributedTo, confidence). * Self-deception is a structural configuration: roleDeceiver = roleDeceived, avowed vs tacit sub-vantage. * The licensed-falsehood safety property (fiction, satire, sarcasm) is modelled via gmeow:veridicalityLicensedFalsehood, keeping these forms distinct from deception. * DL-clean by construction (Principle 3): all new properties are simple ObjectProperties, no transitivity/chain/inverse axioms.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/deception

docs.title: GMEOW Employment Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Employment Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/employment CURIE: gmeow:slices/employment

Type: owl:Ontology

Employment relationships, compensation, and career events (the ResumeRDF / Europass / schema.org / ESCO / CTDL superset layer).

STANDPOINT DOCTRINE (#51). Contested facts in the employment slice — disputed tenure, rival role claims, contested termination — are standpoint-indexed claims that COEXIST, none privileged (Principle 9). A contested employment is two gmeow:accordingTo-annotated gmeow:memberOf base triples, or two reified gmeow:Employment relators each carrying gmeow:accordingTo. A withdrawn employment record is modelled with gmeow:displayable false, never deletion (Principle 10). There is NO employment-specific dispute mechanism, no primaryEmployment, no preferredJob — only the cross-cutting #43 facility.

DOCTRINE. * Employment is a Membership: a reified gufo:Relator connecting an agent to an organization, optionally founded on an Agreement (Principle 4). * Employment events (hiring, promotion, transfer, resignation, termination) are value individuals in the EventType vocabulary, never subclasses (Principle 9). * Employment type (full-time, part-time, contract, intern) is an open value vocabulary, never a subclass taxonomy. * Compensation is a MonetaryAmount with explicit currency ReferenceFrame (Principle 11). * Seniority is an open value vocabulary, orthogonal to employment type and role. * Flat-first, reify on demand: a flat gmeow:memberOf covers the 80% case; promote to gmeow:Employment when type, compensation, seniority, or provenance matters. * Reuse: Membership, Role, Occupation, Agreement, Event/Participation, MonetaryAmount, Credential, Skill, LanguageProficiency.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/employment

docs.title: GMEOW Events Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Events Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/events CURIE: gmeow:slices/events

Type: owl:Ontology

The universal event slice: a temporal occurrence in which entities participate IN ROLES, over POSSIBLY FUZZY time, at POSSIBLY SEVERAL locations, along POSSIBLE trajectories, with POSSIBLE spacetime slices, asserted by POSSIBLY CONFLICTING sources. Supersets schema.org Event, CIDOC-CRM E5/E7/E92, OWL-Time, PROV-O Activity, iCalendar VEVENT, LODE, SEM and Wikidata by reference.

DOCTRINE (the no-mess rules). * Type is a VALUE, not a class: gmeow:Event is one class; the kind is gmeow:eventType (an open value vocabulary of gmeow:EventType individuals), mirroring placeType / Gender / Language. No event-type subclass taxonomy (Principle 9 — no overtyping). * Role is a VALUE on a relator, not a subproperty: participation is reified as gmeow:Participation (the NameUsage / IdentityFacet idiom), and the role is a gmeow:ParticipantRole value — never a hasWitness-style subproperty. * Four orthogonal axes, no inferential bridge: eventType ⟂ participationRole ⟂ temporal ⟂ location. * Flat-first, reify on demand: a flat gmeow:hasParticipant covers the 80% case; promote to a gmeow:Participation when role / period / confidence / evidence is needed (the hasMet / InterpersonalRelationship duality). * Co-equal conflicting claims coexist: no primary date / canonical occurrence; competing dates, types and roles are confidence-weighted, standpoint-indexed statements (consume the standpoint module, #43), never one ground truth. Corrections use gmeow:displayable false, never deletion (Principle 10). * DL-clean time (Principle 3): base-triple datatypes are xsd:dateTime, never xsd:date; fuzzy / approximate time is carried by gmeow:earliestStart / gmeow:latestEnd bounds + a gmeow:temporalPrecision value, not a free-text date.

This module ABSORBS the former genealogy event hierarchy (Principle 6 — refactor forward): the ~30 gmeow:LifeEvent subclasses became gmeow:eventType value individuals and the hasPrincipal / hasWitness / hasOfficiant subproperties became gmeow:ParticipantRole values.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/events

docs.title: GMEOW Evidence Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Evidence Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/evidence CURIE: gmeow:slices/evidence

Type: owl:Ontology

Evidential warrant and source-typing substrate: two orthogonal axes that travel with the evidence link (CitationAct / EvidenceSpan) rather than the asserted fact.

Axis A — Evidential warrant (strength/kind of evidence for a fact). An open value vocabulary gmeow:EvidenceClass reached by a non-functional property gmeow:hasEvidenceClass. A multi-source claim legitimately carries several evidence classes (Principle 9).

Axis B — Source independence and coverage typing (for notability, not truth). Four properties on the citation: gmeow:sourceIndependence, gmeow:sourceTier, gmeow:coverageDepth, and gmeow:supportsNotability. These are explicitly orthogonal to evidential warrant: a primary legal filing may verify a fact (high warrant) without establishing notability (supportsNotability false).

CONSTITUTIONAL GROUNDING: P1 (no SOTA vocabulary unifies these axes), P5 (maximal bridging by reference to CRMinf, PROV-O, schema.org, C2PA, DataCite, nanopublications, WP:GNG), P9 (co-equal facets, no privileged single winner), P10 (suppression by projection, never erasure), P12 (eligibility decisions live in the solver layer).

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/evidence

docs.title: GMEOW Expertise Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Expertise Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/expertise CURIE: gmeow:slices/expertise

Type: owl:Ontology

Skills, occupations and credentials (the schema.org / ESCO / CTDL / O*NET / SOC superset layer). SKOS concepts are reused as recommended value vocabularies rather than re-grounded.

DOCTRINE. * Skill proficiency is reified as a gufo:Relator (gmeow:SkillProficiency) that binds {agent} × {skill} × {level} × {scale} × {interval}, mirroring languages' gmeow:LanguageProficiency and reusing the same gmeow:ProficiencyScale / gmeow:ProficiencyLevel value vocabularies (Principle 6). * Flat-first: gmeow:hasSkill is the 80 % shortcut; promote to SkillProficiency when level, scale, temporal scope, or standpoint matters. * Credential verification is routed through gmeow:Attestation (attestation.ttl), already aligned to vc:VerifiableCredential; expertise supplies the credential content, attestation the signed envelope (Principle 4). * Endorsement of a skill claim is an attestation over a SkillProficiency; contested levels coexist as standpoint-indexed claims (Principle 9). * Occupation classification codes (ESCO, SOC, O*NET) are open literal values on gmeow:occupationClassification; resolution is solver-side (Principle 12).

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/expertise

docs.title: GMEOW Finance Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Finance Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/finance CURIE: gmeow:slices/finance

Type: owl:Ontology

Personal and SMB financial existence: accounts, monetary amounts, transactions, ledgers, invoices, orders, asset holdings, and crypto wallets. Grounded in the existing Event/Participation/Agreement/Rights/Trust substrate. FIBO, schema.org, ISO 4217, ISO 20022, FIGI and OFX are aligned by reference, never imported.

DOCTRINE. * A financial account is an InformationObject (consistent with OnlineAccount): it is fundamentally an information construct — an IBAN, account number, and balance record. The legal/contractual aspect is modelled separately via Agreement (account terms between holder and bank). * Money is a MonetaryAmount = amount (xsd:decimal) + currency (ReferenceFrame individual). DL-clean; no arithmetic in OWL. * Currency is a ReferenceFrame in the frameRealmCurrency realm (Principle 11 — frame-relativity). Each ISO 4217 code is a ReferenceFrame individual. * accountCurrency is NON-FUNCTIONAL: a single FinancialAccount may hold balances in several currencies (multi-currency fintech accounts). The functional constraint moves to Posting/Holding relators. * A transaction is a reified Event (REA pattern): money movement with Agent participants in roles (payer / payee / intermediary) — reuse Event/Participation, never re-mint. * Double-entry as structure: LedgerAccount (asset / liability / equity / revenue / expense — open vocab), JournalEntry ⊑ Event, Posting ⊑ gufo:Relator (account × amount × debit/credit); balance (Σ debits = Σ credits) enforced by SHACL, not OWL. * Loans are Agreements; invoices are Documents; ownership is rights; banks are Organizations; wallets hold trust keys — reuse, don't duplicate. * Open value vocabularies, no overtyping (Principle 9): account types, transaction types, transaction statuses, ledger account types, posting directions, asset types, invoice statuses, order statuses, and payment methods are individuals, never subclasses. * Flat-first, reify on demand: a flat accountBalance on FinancialAccount covers the 80% case; promote to a Holding relator when cost-basis, period, or provenance matters. * Sensitive: P9/P10 + provenance. Reversed/voided transactions are displayable false, retained as the audit trail, never deleted; disputed amounts coexist accordingTo; every figure carries confidence/wasAttributedTo.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/finance

docs.title: GMEOW Gender Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Gender Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/gender CURIE: gmeow:slices/gender

Type: owl:Ontology

A respectful, inclusive model of a person's gender, grounded on a shared gmeow:IdentityFacet — a reified, SELF-ASSERTED claim (a gufo:Relator, the same idiom as names' NameUsage) that mediates a person and an identity value, carrying an optional validity period and the gmeow:displayable display control. This module covers gender IDENTITY, gender EXPRESSION, and the recorded sex-assigned-at-birth datum; the sibling sexuality module reuses the same IdentityFacet base for sexual/romantic orientation. GOVERNING TENETS: (1) ADDRESS ≠ IDENTITY — pronouns and honorifics (in the names module) are how a person is addressed and carry NO inferential bridge to gender; nothing infers one from the other. (2) SEX ≠ GENDER — gmeow:sexAssignedAtBirth is a recorded administrative datum, NOT an IdentityFacet and never equated with gender identity/expression. (3) SELF-ASSERTION is the top authority (gmeow:selfAsserted). (4) CO-EQUALITY — a person may bear many co-equal identities (e.g. bigender = two facets); there is deliberately NO preferred/primary gender term; only display SUPPRESSION (gmeow:displayable false, the deadname analog for a superseded label) is modelled, never deletion. (5) INCLUSIVE WITHOUT OVERTYPING — gmeow:Gender, gmeow:GenderExpressionStyle and gmeow:SexAssignedAtBirth are OPEN value vocabularies of individuals (never per-value Person subclasses, never a forced enum); an identity not among the seeds is expressed by minting a FRESH value individual carrying rdfs:label, the names' custom-PronounSet idiom — there is deliberately no parallel flat-literal shortcut. Aligns (lossily) to GSSO, Homosaurus, schema.org, Wikidata, FOAF and HL7/FHIR; the reified self-asserted-co-equal machinery is canonical.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/gender

docs.title: GMEOW Genealogy Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Genealogy Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/genealogy CURIE: gmeow:slices/genealogy

Type: owl:Ontology

A comprehensive, evidence-centric genealogy model: reified, typed kinship relationships and kinship convenience properties. Life events themselves are modelled by the universal events module (gmeow:Event + gmeow:eventType value vocabulary + the gmeow:Participation relator); a person's life events are gmeow:LifeEvent occurrences carrying gmeow:eventTypeBirth / …Marriage / …NameChange etc. Structured naming terms (gmeow:PersonName et al.) live in the names module and link to the event that confers them via gmeow:conferredByEvent. Supersedes the unmaintained W3C SWAP gedcom vocabulary; aligned to BIO, GEDCOM X, schema.org, Wikidata, REL and GeoNames.

STANDPOINT DOCTRINE (#51). Contested facts in genealogy — disputed parentage, conflicting birth/death dates, competing civil vs parish records — are standpoint-indexed claims that COEXIST, none privileged (Principle 9). A contested birth date is two standpoint-indexed gmeow:eventTime claims on the same gmeow:LifeEvent (the events module's mechanism). A contested parentage is two gmeow:accordingTo-annotated gmeow:hasParent claims, or two reified gmeow:ParentChildRelationship instances each carrying gmeow:accordingTo. There is NO genealogy-specific dispute mechanism, no preferredParent, no primaryKinship — only the cross-cutting #43 facility. A withdrawn parentage claim (an opened-then-closed StandpointTenure, or a superseded claim) sets gmeow:displayable false, never deletion (Principle 10).

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/genealogy

docs.title: GMEOW GraphRAG Module
docs.text:
Pipeline observability for retrieval-augmented and GraphRAG systems (#54 facets A/B/F): the corpus, embedding, index, and retrieval substrate, and the derived entity-graph artifacts (extracted entities/relationships, communities, community summaries) — every artifact content-addressed, every step an attributed activity, so the derived graph is AUDITABLE and revisable rather than a black box (GraphRAG, arXiv:2404.16130). Claims extracted by the pipeline are the CORE ai slice's business (a StandpointClaim with model vantage); this extension carries the machinery around them. Vector payloads stay outside the graph by reference (P12).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/graphrag CURIE: gmeow:slices/graphrag

Type: owl:Ontology

Per-result epistemics (a retrieval's score for ONE chunk) ride RDF 1.2 statement annotations on the gmeow:retrievedChunk triple (gmeow:retrievalScore) — competing re-ranker scores coexist attributed, never overwritten (P9, P3).

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/graphrag

docs.title: GMEOW GTS Transport Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW GTS Transport Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/gts CURIE: gmeow:slices/gts

Type: owl:Ontology

Transport/packaging vocabulary so GMEOW can DESCRIBE and dogfood its own transport: a GTS file (docs/GTS-SPEC.md) as a first-class entity — its segments, profiles, chain heads, transform codecs, opaque (sealed/undecodable) frames, and compaction lineage.

MODEL BOUNDARIES (Principles 1, 9, 12). - GTS gives TRANSPORT claims (these bytes, this order, this chain); GMEOW gives CONTENT claims (this statement is true, according to whom). A frame signature or head commitment is an Attestation whose attestedSubject is a GTSSegment; it proves bytes/order/signer key control, never the truth of the carried statements (#342). - Compaction re-authors only the ORDERING: content claims ride as ordinary quads and are rewrite-invariant by construction; transport claims over the old chain become detached evidence about the source document, cited through the compaction's derivation lineage. - Fold semantics, codec reversal, hash verification, and signature checking live in the solver layer (the gts engines); this module only describes their artifacts and outcomes.

REUSE (no parallel mechanisms — #267). - Byte identity of blobs and files -> gmeow:contentDigest (sources). - Chain-head identity of a segment -> gmeow:gtsHeadId, a versionFingerprint (versions). - Frame/head signatures, signers -> gmeow:hasSignature / gmeow:Attestation (attestation). - Compaction and production lineage -> gmeow:wasGeneratedBy / wasDerivedFrom (provenance). - Suppress frames -> gmeow:displayable (kernel, P10) — suppression is a display overlay, never erasure, in the format AND in the ontology. - annot-frame standpoints -> gmeow:accordingTo / standpointModality (standpoint). - Media payloads -> gmeow:MediaObject (documents) carried as blobs.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/gts

docs.title: GMEOW Images Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Images Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/images CURIE: gmeow:slices/images

Type: owl:Ontology

The Images super-ontology — a layered model for contextual depiction, region encoding, scene graphs, and technical metadata (issue #22). Builds on the WEMI spine (#208): a visual work is a gmeow:Work with workTypeVisual / workTypePhotographic; the digital file is a gmeow:Manifestation (gmeow:MediaObject) plus gmeow:Item / hasCarrier. Colourspace is carried via gmeow:hasReferenceFrame (#70). Rights reuse the #21 facility directly.

LAYERS. 1. Contextual depiction — the DepictionUsage relator (mirrors NameUsage) and the flat gmeow:depicts shortcut (⊑ gmeow:isAbout). 2. Region encoding — ImageRegion + RegionSelector with an open SelectorType value vocabulary (SVG, pixel rectangle, fractional, polygon, RLE, COCO, DICOM-SEG, Web Annotation fragment). 3. Region / UI rendering — IIIF Presentation API 3 projections (Canvas, Annotation, selector mapping). No new ontology terms; purely projection. 4. Spatial context / scene graphs — SceneGraphEdge relator binding two ImageRegions with a SceneRelationType value (leftOf, rightOf, inside, holding, wearing, etc.). 5. Hardware / technical metadata — pixelWidth, pixelHeight, imageOrientation, captureTime, captureDevice, colourspace (gmeow:colourspace ⊑ gmeow:hasReferenceFrame) on MediaObject in documents.ttl. 6. Provenance / workflow — image-specific eventType values (capture, scanning, processing, annotation) in events.ttl; reuse wasGeneratedBy / wasDerivedFrom. 7. Rights / IP — reuse #21 terms directly. 8. SEO / discovery — schema.org ImageObject projections.

GOVERNING TENETS. * No flat gmeow:depicts as a contact field — it is a formally defined image ontology property, subproperty of gmeow:isAbout, domain MediaObject. * No primary / preferred depiction (Principle 9). Co-equal depictions coexist; a superseded one sets gmeow:displayable false (Principle 10). * Selector encoding kinds are an open value vocabulary; actual mask parsing / coordinate conversion lives in the solver layer (Principle 12). * All alignments are by reference (Principle 5): schema.org, IIIF, W3C Web Annotation, W3C EXIF Ontology, XMP, IPTC, CIDOC-CRM/CRMdig.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/images

docs.title: GMEOW Language Core Module
docs.text:
The slim language foundation every slice depends on: the Language and WritingSystem classes, the private-use/BCP-47 tag machinery, and the seed Language individuals that anchor the framework's own literals.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/language CURIE: gmeow:slices/language

Type: owl:Ontology

The CORE half of the languages split (#287 dependency surgery): gmeow:Language and gmeow:WritingSystem as first-class, registry-independent classes; gmeow:languageTag / gmeow:bcp47Tag / gmeow:languageCode (the x-gmeow-* private-use anchor machinery); and the three seed individuals — English, Mandarin, French — that back the framework's own language-tagged literals (Canadian + US + European + Chinese coverage). The rich sociolinguistic machinery (proficiency, writing-system usage, varieties, diachronic states, version lineage, conlangs) lives in the languages extension slice, which extends these classes.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/language

docs.title: GMEOW Languages Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Languages Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/languages CURIE: gmeow:slices/languages

Type: owl:Ontology

Languages and writing systems as first-class, registry-INDEPENDENT information objects (the BCP-47 / ISO 639 / Glottolog / Wikidata / schema.org superset layer). A gmeow:Language has a self-minted IRI; codes (gmeow:languageCode, gmeow:authorityLink, skos:exactMatch) are OPTIONAL alignments, never identity — so a code-less conlang (Ithkuil), a fast-versioning AI-minted interlingua, an under-coded sign/minority language, and a programming language are all co-equal first-class languages. Covers natural, constructed (auxiliary/engineered/artistic/ritual), AI-generated, historical/reconstructed, sign/whistled/tactile, and formal/programming/markup languages. Writing systems are first-class and a language CO-MINGLES many co-equal scripts (Japanese = kanji/Hani + hiragana/Hira + katakana/Kana + rōmaji/Latn), bound by the reified gmeow:WritingSystemUsage relator (mirroring names' gmeow:NameUsage), which also models script changes over time (Turkish Arabic→Latin, 1928). Versions form a first-class lineage (gmeow:versionOf / supersedes). Endonym/exonym names reuse the names module's gmeow:Appellation; transliteration schemes that produce a gmeow:romanization are named by gmeow:transliterationScheme and catalogued as FnO functions in the projection layer.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/languages

docs.title: GMEOW Lexicon Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Lexicon Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/lexicon CURIE: gmeow:slices/lexicon

Type: owl:Ontology

Lexical items, forms, usage attestations, and etymological derivations — the lexical and constructional layer of GMEOW. Models words, morphemes, phrases, idioms, symbols, and constructions as first-class information objects, with concrete forms (written, spoken, signed, reconstructed, transliterated, translated) and evidence-backed attestations. Etymology is modeled as a graph of provenance-rich, standpointed claims, not as a flat origin string (Principle 9). Aligns to OntoLex-Lemon by reference (Principle 5). Builds on the language-state/variety layer in #170 and the universal observation stack (#43).

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/lexicon

docs.text:

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/lifecycle CURIE: gmeow:slices/lifecycle

Type: owl:Ontology

Universal time-bounded existence facility: ontic existence-over-time for any gmeow:Entity, distinct from suppression (a display contract). Every entity may carry creation and destruction events, an existence interval, and supersession links. Revised forward, never deleted (Principle 10). Reuses the events module (gmeow:Event + EventType value vocabulary), the temporal module (TimeInterval / TimeScopedRelation / validFrom / validUntil), and the standpoint module (accordingTo / contested claims). Flat-first, reify on demand.

docs.title: GMEOW Names Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Names Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/names CURIE: gmeow:slices/names

Type: owl:Ontology

A universal, multi-culture, inclusive naming model (the schema.org / vCard N / GEDCOM X NameForm / W3C pronouns superset layer). A name is never a bare attribute: it is a reified gmeow:Appellation (an information object with structured, typed parts) borne by an entity, and gmeow:NameUsage is the gufo:Relator binding {who is named} × {which appellation} × {by/among whom} × {register} × {period} — so 'Aunt Genny' (intimate, family audience) is distinct from 'Mrs Smith' (formal) without privileging either. Name-part kinds, purposes, registers, pronoun sets and honorifics are open VALUE vocabularies, so patronymic, Arabic ism/kunya/nasab/laqab/nisba, Spanish double surname, East-Asian family-first and courtesy names, Tamil initial-expansion and mononym are all expressible without forcing a Western given+family order. GOVERNING TENET — co-equality (anti-colonial naming): a person's names in different languages/scripts (e.g. Patrick Colm Audley and 欧德理) are CO-EQUAL full names; none is the other's alternateName or romanization, none is 'primary'. There is deliberately NO preferredForDisplay / primaryName term — display SELECTION is locale-relative and symmetric; only display SUPPRESSION (gmeow:displayable false, e.g. a deadname) is modelled. Pronouns and honorifics are sex/gender INDEPENDENT — ADDRESS (what you want to be called) is not IDENTITY (what you are): they are never inferred from, nor do they imply, gmeow:hasGenderIdentity / gmeow:hasGenderExpression / gmeow:sexAssignedAtBirth / orientation (modelled in the gender + sexuality modules). Follows the W3C 'Personal names around the world' guidance.

STANDPOINT DOCTRINE (#51). Contested facts in the naming slice — endonym vs exonym per community, a name disputed by two authorities, a community-specific exonym that another standpoint refutes — are standpoint-indexed claims that COEXIST, none privileged (Principle 9). A contested name-usage is two gmeow:NameUsage instances each carrying gmeow:accordingTo, or two gmeow:accordingTo-annotated gmeow:hasName statements. CRITICAL DISTINCTION: gmeow:usageAudience is who the name is used TOWARD (the social scope); gmeow:usageAuthority / gmeow:accordingTo is who ASSERTS the name-usage claim (the standpoint frame). A community's endonym may be both audience and standpoint, but the axes are orthogonal and must not be conflated. There is NO naming-specific dispute mechanism, no preferredName, no primaryAppellation — only the cross-cutting #43 facility. Superseded names (deadnames, former legal names) set gmeow:displayable false, never deletion (Principle 10).

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/names

docs.title: GMEOW Narrative Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Narrative Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/narrative CURIE: gmeow:slices/narrative

Type: owl:Ontology

Narrative reference frames and creative-work sourcing. Part of the #42 Location-as-reference-frame epic.

DOCTRINE. * A NarrativeReferenceFrame is a ReferenceFrame (canon supplies coordinate topology for in-universe locations, dates, and events) and functionally serves as the standpoint under which in-universe claims hold true, without subclassing gmeow:Standpoint (gUFO MixIden enforces exactly-one-Kind inheritance). * CreativeWorks (BookRelease, SerialInstallment) remain out-of-universe rights-bearing artifacts; they source, witness, or revise a narrative frame via gmeow:sourceFor. * Characters, places, organizations, events, artifacts in a narrative are ordinary GMEOW entities whose claims are scoped gmeow:accordingTo the narrative frame. * Cross-continuity variants are linked with gmeow:counterpartOf, never merged (Principle 5). * Retcons and canon revisions are preserved as coexisting frame-scoped claims with gmeow:supersedes and gmeow:displayable false (Principle 10). * No single canon wins (Principle 9): competing continuities coexist as separate NarrativeReferenceFrames that may sharpen one another.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/narrative

docs.title: GMEOW Norms Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Norms Module — generalized deontics with indexed authority (issues #351 / #352, EPIC #348).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/norms CURIE: gmeow:slices/norms

Type: owl:Ontology

Generalized deontics with indexed authority — the constitutional keystone of the normative stack (EPIC #348).

DOCTRINE. * THERE IS NO OUGHT, ONLY OUGHT-ACCORDING-TO. Every norm names its issuer (gmeow:normIssuer); an ought without an issuer is the deontic analogue of a global truth axiom and is forbidden by SHACL. Two contradictory normative systems coexist without inconsistency because neither is asserted — both are recorded as issued (Principles 1, 9; the deception module's held/projected move applied to oughts). normIssuer ⊑ gmeow:accordingTo is documented, not axiomatised, because accordingTo is an AnnotationProperty and normIssuer is an ObjectProperty — the vantage ⊑ accordingTo precedent (standpoint module). * PRECEDENCE IS DATA, NOT SEMANTICS. gmeow:overrides is pairwise and deliberately NOT transitive: lex-superior chains are solver inferences, never reasoner entailments. AuthorityLevel is an ordered value vocabulary (the kernel GranularityLevel pattern — third use); ordering comparisons are solver work (Principle 12). 'Tier 2 overrode X until v3.5' is a gmeow:PrecedenceTenure — the StandpointTenure idiom (Principle 10: withdrawal by suppression, never deletion). * CONDITIONS ARE STORED, NEVER EXECUTED. A gmeow:Condition is an InformationObject whose canonical form is prose (conditionText); formalizations (SPARQL ASK, CEL, Rego, Cedar, XACML, SHACL) attach as ConditionExpressions, and EACH FORMALIZATION IS A CLAIM of equivalence to the prose, challengeable through the statement layer. Whether a condition held is a gmeow:ConditionEvaluation — a vantage-indexed Observation — never a graph entailment. No CI step, test, or tool may evaluate a ConditionExpression against the graph as part of validation (the Principle 12 boundary made operational; see docs.md). * THE RIGHTS GRAFT (#352) lands here, extension-side, with ZERO core churn: gmeow:Rule ⊑ gmeow:Norm plus subproperty grafts. The deontic trio (Permission / Prohibition / Duty) is NOT an inferior duplicate of Norm + deonticModality — it is a rigid subkind partition (fixed modality per subkind) under the open modality axis, kept for the asset case and its projection affordances. When this extension is absent, the core rights slice behaves exactly as before. * Deontic force ranges over teleology: gmeow:prescribedConduct points at event types, goals (#350), situations, or rights actions; its range is intentionally open (the tenurePosition precedent) so the graft needs no dual-typing and the generated schema surface keeps a clean property. * ALIGNMENTS DEFERRED to the compiler-arc window (the wip-aboutness-349 precedent): ODRL 2.2 (EDOAL — odrl:Constraint ↔ Condition is structural), LegalRuleML ( ↔ overrides/PrecedenceTenure — the one target where precedence survives round-trip), LKIF-Core, DPV, SUMO normative attributes, UFO-L. Target list is fixed in #351.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/norms

docs.title: GMEOW Notation and Symbolic Systems Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Notation and Symbolic Systems Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/notation CURIE: gmeow:slices/notation

Type: owl:Ontology

Symbolic systems, notation systems, and their usage — the representational layer beneath and alongside natural/formal languages. Models mathematical notation, musical notation, emoji conventions, gesture systems, stenography, cryptographic encodings, and other non-alphabetic symbol systems as first-class information objects. A symbolic system is NOT a language by default; a standpointed claim may reclassify it (Principle 9). Builds on the languages module (#169) and the lexicon module (#171).

docs.title: GMEOW Observations Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Observations Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/observations CURIE: gmeow:slices/observations

Type: owl:Ontology

The universal observation stack: a reified gufo:Relator that unifies spatial measurement, temporal dating, sensory reading, standpoint claims, identity claims, naming claims, rights claims, and kinship claims into one structure — realising Governing Principle #9 (Observation ≡ Measurement ≡ Standpoint ≡ IdentityFacet ≡ NameUsage ≡ RightsStatement ≡ KinRelationship). Sits in the foundational provenance/standpoint layer and is consumed by every slice. Aligns SOSA/SSN, PROV-O, and CIDOC E13 by reference.

Also home to the universal Quantity / MeasuredValue construct (#77): a scalar numeric value bundled with unit/frame, determinacy, and provenance — the synthesis of FRAME-GEN + DET-GEN + OBS. gmeow:Quantity and gmeow:MeasuredValue are equivalent to gmeow:ScalarQuantity, providing domain-neutral names for the same construct.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/observations

docs.title: GMEOW Organization Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Organization Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/organization CURIE: gmeow:slices/organization

Type: owl:Ontology

Organizational roles and memberships (the ORG-superset layer).

STANDPOINT DOCTRINE (#51). Contested facts in the organization slice — disputed membership, rival succession claims, contested recognition of legitimacy — are standpoint-indexed claims that COEXIST, none privileged (Principle 9). A contested membership is two gmeow:accordingTo-annotated gmeow:memberOf base triples, or two reified gmeow:Membership relators each carrying gmeow:accordingTo. A contested succession (post-merger, post-coup) is two gmeow:accordingTo-annotated gmeow:subOrganizationOf claims. Recognition granted and later withdrawn is modelled as a gmeow:StandpointTenure with gmeow:displayable false, never deletion (Principle 10). There is NO organization-specific dispute mechanism, no primaryMember, no preferredSuccessor — only the cross-cutting #43 facility.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/organization

docs.title: GMEOW Locations Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Locations Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places CURIE: gmeow:slices/places

Type: owl:Ontology

Locations — geographic places, online (virtual) locations, digital storage locations, celestial / astronomical locations, and biological-sequence loci — with coordinates, geometry, containment, and external-gazetteer coreference (the schema.org / GeoSPARQL / GeoNames / Getty TGN / Wikidata / WGS84 / BOT / ifcOWL / IVOA / UAT / SWEET / FALDO / Sequence Ontology superset layer). Place kinds, celestial object kinds, and sequence feature kinds are open value vocabularies (gmeow:placeType, gmeow:celestialObjectType, gmeow:sequenceFeatureType), so any granularity from country to room, from star to galaxy cluster, or from chromosome to SNP, can be a first-class, QID-bearing entity chained by containedInPlace or locatedAt.

STANDPOINT DOCTRINE (#51). Contested facts in the locations slice — sovereignty/jurisdiction disputes, competing place names (endonym vs exonym per community), boundary changes, regulatory overlays — are standpoint-indexed claims that COEXIST, none privileged (Principle 9). A contested sovereignty claim (e.g. Crimea-class) is two gmeow:accordingTo-annotated gmeow:containedInPlace base triples. A contested toponym is two gmeow:accordingTo-annotated gmeow:hasPlaceName statements, or two reified gmeow:PlaceNaming instances each carrying gmeow:accordingTo. gmeow:usageAuthority on a gmeow:NameUsage names the toponymic authority; gmeow:accordingTo on the same usage names the standpoint frame asserting it — the two axes are orthogonal and must not be conflated. There is NO location-specific dispute mechanism, no preferredJurisdiction, no primaryName — only the cross-cutting #43 facility. Superseded or withdrawn claims set gmeow:displayable false, never deletion (Principle 10).

REGULATORY OVERLAYS (#103 + #93). Legal and regulatory spatial overlays — zoning, protected areas, restricted airspace, sanctions, tax/electoral districts, postal zones, civil-time zones, fishing zones, customs zones, maritime zones (territorial sea, EEZ, continental shelf, high seas, marine protected area), aviation zones (airway, CTR, TMA, FIR, ATZ, MOA, warning, alert), and temporary NOTAM notices — are modelled as reified gmeow:RegulatoryOverlay instances (⊑ gmeow:TimeScopedRelation), each binding a place, an authority, an overlay type (open value vocabulary), and an optional RightsStatement (#21) for the deontic rules. 3D bounds (altitude/depth) are frame-relative ScalarQuantity values in explicit vertical reference frames (Principle 11). Contested overlays (disputed EEZ, overlapping airspace claims) coexist as multiple standpoint-indexed instances, never a single winner (Principle 9).

VIRTUAL LOCATIONS + NETWORK ADDRESS SPACE (#84). Virtual locations (video conferences, chat spaces, websites, social media pages) are typed by an open value vocabulary (gmeow:VirtualLocationType). Their network addresses — IP, IPv6, MAC, DNS, URL, port, BGP-AS — are modelled as frame-relative coordinates (gmeow:NetworkAddress) in topology-only reference frames (gmeow:frameKindTopological) nested under the Internet root frame via gmeow:parentFrame. CIDR containment, DNS resolution, and path-length are solver-layer computations (Principle 12), never asserted as triples in the OWL core.

MATHEMATICAL / n-D REFERENCE FRAMES (#86). Hilbert spaces, smooth manifolds, phase spaces, and latent vector spaces are first-class gmeow:ReferenceFrame instances under gmeow:frameRealmMathematical. A finite-dimensional vector space (ℝⁿ, ℂⁿ, latent embedding) uses one gmeow:Axis with gmeow:hasCoordinateMatrix encoding the full column/row matrix via gmeow:CoordinateMatrix.matrixShape, not n separate axis individuals (Principle 12 — the ontology carries structure, solver carries cardinality). A configuration space (C-space, e.g. 6-DOF robot arm joint angles) uses one axis per joint. A phase space uses paired generalized-coordinate and generalized-momentum axes (qᵢ, pᵢ) and carries gmeow:hasMetricKind gmeow:metricSymplectic. A Hilbert space (∞-D) and latent vector spaces are modelled with gmeow:dimensionCount 1 and a single axis, leaving actual dimensionality to the matrix shape attribute, since the ontology does not assert infinite-dimensional structures as OWL individuals (Principle 12). OpenMath / Content-MathML encoding of coordinates is handled by the value-space layer (gmeow:coordinateValue typed by gmeow:CoordinateEncoding), not by per-expression ontology axioms.

ROBOTIC REALM — C-SPACE / TF / SLAM (#88). Robot configuration spaces (C-space) are modelled as gmeow:ReferenceFrame instances in the gmeow:frameRealmRobotic realm, with joint-angle axes and geodesic metrics on a configuration-space manifold. Task-space and velocity frames are Cartesian seeds under the same realm. The TF transform tree is a hierarchy of nested frames linked via gmeow:parentFrame; static vs dynamic transforms are distinguished by statement-level temporal metadata (statement DSL), not by new ontology properties — the actual homogeneous-transform matrix math lives in the solver layer (Principle 12). SLAM occupancy maps are probabilistic occupancy-grid reference frames hosted by the robot, with gmeow:determinacyProbabilistic and gmeow:confidence carried on the observation results (CoordinateMatrix or SpatialCoordinates), not on the frame itself.

BIOLOGICAL-SEQUENCE REALM — FALDO / SEQUENCE ONTOLOGY / GFF3 (#90). Biological sequences (DNA, RNA, protein) are modelled as gmeow:ReferenceFrame instances in the gmeow:frameRealmBiological realm. A reference assembly (e.g. GRCh38) is a versioned, linear 1-D reference frame with a single position axis; a sequence feature (gene, exon, SNP, CDS) is a gmeow:BiologicalSequenceLocation bearing gmeow:SequenceCoordinates with explicit start, end, and strand in that frame. Feature types are an open value vocabulary (gmeow:sequenceFeatureType) aligned by reference to Sequence Ontology (SO) terms. FALDO positions map to gmeow:SequenceCoordinates; liftover (coordinate conversion between assemblies) is declared via gmeow:transformsTo on the ReferenceFrame but executed by an external solver (Principle 12).

CADASTRAL / LAND ADMINISTRATION REALM — LADM / INSPIRE (#92). Parcels, lots, and spatial units are Places typed by an open value vocabulary (gmeow:placeType). Their boundaries are Geometry / SpatialCoordinates in a terrestrial reference frame. Ownership and land rights (ownership, lease, easement, mortgage, usufruct) are modelled as reified gmeow:LandTenure instances (⊑ gmeow:TimeScopedRelation), each binding a place, a party (Agent), a rights statement (#21), and a tenure type (open value vocabulary). A structured cadastral identifier (folio, title, lot, parcel ID) is modelled as a reified gmeow:CadastralReference (⊑ gmeow:InformationObject) linked to the place. Boundary surveys carry determinacy (typically crisp for surveyed boundaries, disputed for contested claims). Contested titles coexist as multiple standpoint-indexed LandTenures, none privileged (Principle 9). Expired or lapsed tenures keep their record with gmeow:displayable false, never deletion (Principle 10). Area and intersection computations stay in the solver layer (Principle 12). Aligns ISO 19152 LADM and INSPIRE Cadastral Parcels by reference (SSSOM).

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: GMEOW Procedures Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Procedures Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/procedures CURIE: gmeow:slices/procedures

Type: owl:Ontology

The plan ⟂ execution slice: a prescriptive layer that de-conflates procedures, recipes, protocols, and workflow definitions from the events that enact them. Reuses the event stack (Execution ⊑ Event, Participation for agent/tool assignment), the information-object stack (Procedure / ProcedureStep ⊑ InformationObject), and the temporal stack (Allen relations over Execution occurrences). ControlFlow and DataFlow are reified relators following the Participation idiom.

DOCTRINE. * Plan ⟂ execution: a Procedure is an InformationObject (prescriptive spec); an Execution is an Event (occurrence that enacts it). One recipe, many prepared meals; one protocol, many runs. * Type is a VALUE, not a class: ProcedureType / StepType / BranchConditionType / ExecutionStatus are open value vocabularies of individuals (Principle 9 — no overtyping). * Recursive composition: a ProcedureStep may reference a subprocess Procedure via gmeow:stepEnactsProcedure; subProcedureOf provides Procedure-to-Procedure mereology. * Step ordering at the plan level is via ControlFlow relators (with optional flowOrder); at the execution level, Allen relations (before, meets, …) order the actual Event occurrences (Principle 12 — compute outside the logic). * Branch guard evaluation is solver-side: the guard condition type is recorded as a BranchConditionType value on the ControlFlow relator; the actual evaluation stays in the solver / SHACL layer (Principle 12). * Flat-first, reify on demand: a flat gmeow:executionParticipant covers the 80% case; promote to a gmeow:Participation when role / period / confidence / evidence is needed. * Two seed profiles demonstrate the generalisation: an ingestion-process profile (superseding the "source-packet bundle" idea) and a research-inquiry profile (superseding the flat research-queue).

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/procedures

Type: owl:Ontology

Cross-cutting data-quality layer refining confidence and provenance across every realm. Quality assessments are reified observations about ISO 19157 dimensions (positional accuracy, temporal accuracy, thematic accuracy, completeness, logical consistency, topological consistency) plus lineage. Aligns W3C DQV and GeoDCAT-AP by reference; quality-metric computation lives in the solver layer (Principle 12).

QualityAssessment reuses the universal Observation stack: the assessed entity is the observedFeature, the quality result is the observationResult (typically a ScalarQuantity), and the assessment method is the observationMethod. This keeps the quality layer thin and consistent with every other GMEOW claim construct.

docs.title: GMEOW Rights & IP Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Rights & IP Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/rights CURIE: gmeow:slices/rights

Type: owl:Ontology

Cross-cutting, foundational, INSTANCE-level rights / IP / trademark / licensing facility (#21) — the machine-readable rights superset layer (ODRL, CC REL, dcterms, schema.org, RightsStatements.org, WIPO). Distinct from the ontology-ALIGNMENT license policy in src/gmeow_tools/config.py (LinkPolicy / policy_for_license), which governs whether an external vocabulary's AXIOMS may be copied INTO GMEOW; this module governs the rights of the INSTANCES GMEOW describes. It generalises the metadata-level dcterms:license / dc:rights on the root ontology to arbitrary works, images, brands, software and data. The Images super-ontology and the Employment / publication block build on it, so it ships first.

DOCTRINE. * A licence IS an agreement (gmeow:License ⊑ gmeow:Agreement) — it reuses gmeow:hasParty (specialised by gmeow:licensor / gmeow:licensee), never a parallel party model. * Rights holders ARE agents: holder attribution reuses gmeow:wasAttributedTo (specialised by gmeow:copyrightHolder / gmeow:trademarkHolder), never a duplicate hasHolder. * Rights-bearing things are gmeow:CreativeWork / gmeow:InformationObject; the facility attaches there, not at gmeow:Entity at large. * Reify-on-demand (Principle 4): a flat gmeow:hasLicense / gmeow:hasCopyright covers the common case; the gmeow:RightsStatement relator + the ODRL-superset deontic trio (Permission / Prohibition / Duty over a gmeow:RightsAction value) is promoted when permissions, prohibitions or duties must be expressed. * Maximal superset, by reference (Principle 5): GMEOW mints one canonical term per concept and aligns it to ODRL / CC REL / dcterms / schema.org / WIPO / RightsStatements.org / PREMIS — never imports an external axiom. The machine-readable ODRL policy, the CC REL licence, and the schema.org rights cluster are GENERATED projections (queries/projections/odrl.rq, cc.rq, schema-org.rq). * Suppression, never erasure (Principle 10): an expired / lapsed / cancelled right keeps its record (gmeow:trademarkStatusExpired, validUntil) and is suppressed for display, never deleted. * Open value vocabularies, no overtyping (Principle 9): the kinds of action, licence family, trademark status and copyright status are OPEN individuals, never per-value subclasses, and there is no preferred / primary right. * DL-clean (Principle 3): year / notice / credit datatypes are rdfs:Literal in the TBox (xsd:gYear / xsd:date are not OWL 2 DL datatypes); typed literals live in data, which is outside the reasoned closure.

REUSE. gmeow:Agreement / gmeow:hasParty (agreements), gmeow:wasAttributedTo / gmeow:wasDerivedFrom (provenance), gmeow:CreativeWork / gmeow:InformationObject / gmeow:Agent (documents / core), gmeow:validFrom / gmeow:validUntil (temporal), gmeow:confidence (provenance). See docs/rights.md and docs/rights-mapping.md.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/rights

docs.title: GMEOW Risk Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Risk Module — hazards, type-level causation, cascades, and mitigations (issue #354, EPIC #348).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/risk CURIE: gmeow:slices/risk

Type: owl:Ontology

Hazards, type-level causation, cascades, and mitigations — counterfactual causal structure without counterfactual machinery.

DOCTRINE. * THE COUNTERFACTUAL PROBLEM DISSOLVES AT THE TYPE LEVEL: cascades relate event TYPES, never event instances — nothing in this slice asserts that anything occurred, and the no-occurrence gate makes that executable (loading the full fixture set entails zero gmeow:Event instances from this slice's terms). 'Trust betrayal dissolves the bond' is a claim about kinds of events; the catastrophe it warns of need never have happened. PROV lineage and CRM influence are token-level; OBO RO is the rare type-level causation vocabulary — that asymmetry is why this slice exists. * CAUSAL LINKS ARE CLAIMS LIKE ANY OTHER: standpoint-indexed and confidence-bearing through the statement layer. Two risk analysts disagreeing about whether T1 promotes T2 are two coexisting claims (Principle 9). Cascade propagation, probability composition, and simulation are solver work over the recorded links (Principle 12); gmeow:linkStrength is solver INPUT, never solver output written back as assertion. * FIRST gufo:Disposition USE IN GMEOW: a Hazard is a bearer's disposition toward harm, manifested (when it manifests at all) as events of a feared type. Inherence is asserted with GMEOW's own gmeow:hazardBearer (Principle 5: gufo:inheresIn is the alignment target, not the asserted axiom). * MITIGATION CROSSES TO DEONTICS BY OPEN RANGE: a Mitigation binds a measure — a gmeow:Norm (norms extension) or a Procedure (procedures extension) — to what it counters. The measure range is intentionally open (the tenurePosition precedent, fourth use): the P16 DAG rule bars extension→extension dependencies, and the open range lets the deontic and procedural worlds plug in without axiom coupling. * SEVERITY IS AN ORDERED VOCABULARY (the kernel GranularityLevel pattern — catastrophic ≻ severe ≻ moderate ≻ minor, gmeow:moreSevereThan transitive ON LEVELS ONLY), anchored terminologically to ISO 31000 / IEC 60812 in docs, never in axioms. * ALIGNMENTS DEFERRED to the compiler-arc window: OBO RO causal properties (linkage-only, BFO lineage), MITRE D3FEND (countermeasure ↔ Mitigation), STIX 2.1/ATT&CK, UCO, ConceptNet/ATOMIC rows; projections to bowtie JSON, FMEA CSV, STIX bundles each with declared-loss manifests. Target list fixed in #354.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/risk

docs.title: GMEOW Sexuality Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Sexuality Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/sexuality CURIE: gmeow:slices/sexuality

Type: owl:Ontology

A respectful, inclusive model of a person's orientation, reusing the gmeow:IdentityFacet base from the gender module (a reified, SELF-ASSERTED gufo:Relator). It applies the SPLIT-ATTRACTION model: sexual orientation and romantic orientation are SEPARATE, mutually independent axes — so asexual-biromantic, aromantic-bisexual and similar are directly expressible; neither is inferred from the other, nor from gender identity/expression, sex-assigned-at-birth, pronouns or honorifics. GOVERNING TENETS (shared with gender): self-assertion is the top authority; co-equality (no preferred/primary orientation; superseded labels kept with gmeow:displayable false, never deleted); INCLUSIVE WITHOUT OVERTYPING — gmeow:SexualOrientationValue and gmeow:RomanticOrientationValue are OPEN value vocabularies of individuals (never per-value subclasses, never a forced enum), an orientation not among the seeds being a FRESH value individual with rdfs:label. Aligns (lossily) to GSSO, Homosaurus and Wikidata; schema.org and FOAF have no orientation term, so orientation is a documented lossy drop at the projection layer. The machinery is otherwise canonical.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/sexuality

docs.text:
The GMEOW Software Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/software CURIE: gmeow:slices/software

Type: owl:Ontology

The software slice: a five-facet de-conflation of the project domain.

Project ≠ Product ≠ Codebase ≠ Repository ≠ History.

Each facet is separately identified, separately classed, and never bridged by subclassing or equivalence. DOAP's original sin — collapsing endeavour, product, repo, and history into one class — is corrected here; DOAP is aligned by reference as a lossy downcast, never imported (Principle 5).

REUSE. - Events / Participation / Activity: events.ttl, provenance.ttl - Contribution / ContributionRole: creative-works.ttl - VersionSet / VersionMembership: versions.ttl - Attestation / CryptographicSignature: attestation.ttl, trust.ttl - contentDigest / versionFingerprint: sources.ttl, versions.ttl - Temporal / standpoint / displayable: temporal.ttl, standpoint.ttl, core.ttl

The flat property gmeow:developer is REMOVED (Principle 6 — greenfield); the Contribution relator and hasContributor shortcut supersede it.

docs.title: GMEOW Standpoint Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Standpoint Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/standpoint CURIE: gmeow:slices/standpoint

Type: owl:Ontology

Cross-cutting foundational facility (a peer of the temporal module): the standpoint axis — according to whom a statement is held true. It lands in the statement/provenance layer and is consumed by every slice that records contested facts (events, locations, genealogy, organizations, trust, naming).

DOCTRINE. * Three orthogonal axes, no inferential bridge: gmeow:accordingTo (whose frame) ⟂ gmeow:wasAttributedTo (which source recorded it) ⟂ gmeow:confidence (how sure we are). * Two clocks kept apart: fact-time (gmeow:validFrom / gmeow:validUntil — when the claimed fact holds) ⟂ standpoint-time (when the standpoint held the position — light via validFrom/Until on the statement, heavy via a reified gmeow:StandpointTenure). * No single slot to win (CONSTITUTION Principle 9): a contested fact is several standpoint-indexed claims that coexist; there is no preferredRank / primary* selector. * Suppression, never erasure (Principle 10): a withdrawn claim or a closed tenure sets gmeow:displayable false; it is retained, not deleted. * DL-clean by construction (Principle 3): the standpoint axis is an owl:AnnotationProperty, so the generated OWL downcast stays OWL 2 DL.

FORMAL GROUNDING. The facility realises Standpoint Logic (Gómez Álvarez & Rudolph): gmeow:accordingTo is the axiom-level standpoint label (cf. Standpoint-OWL 2 standpointLabel); gmeow:standpointModality unequivocal / conceivable are the □_S / ◊_S operators; gmeow:sharpens is the standpoint ⊆ / precisification relation; gmeow:universalStandpoint is the universal standpoint *. See docs/standpoints.md.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/standpoint

docs.title: GMEOW Tags Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Tags Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/tags CURIE: gmeow:slices/tags

Type: owl:Ontology

Universal tagging building block — open folksonomy, aboutness, and typing as three distinct axes (Principle 9). A gmeow:Tag is an information-object value (like a skos:Concept); a gmeow:TagScheme is its namespace bucket; and gmeow:Tagging is a gufo:Relator that reifies the act of tagging with provenance, confidence, temporal scope and suppression (Principle 10). The flat gmeow:hasTag shortcut covers the 80% case; promote to Tagging when the act itself must be a node. Tags align (lossily) to SKOS, schema.org, W3C Web Annotation and MOAT.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/tags

docs.title: GMEOW Teleology Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Teleology Module — goals, desires, intentions, and commitments (issue #350, EPIC #348).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/teleology CURIE: gmeow:slices/teleology

Type: owl:Ontology

Goals, desires, intentions, and commitments — the UFO-C intentional-moment trichotomy surfaced as GMEOW core (Principle 16: an agent recording its OWN goals across sessions is a question every AI system will face about itself, alongside identity and deception epistemics).

DOCTRINE. * The trichotomy is commitment-graded: a Desire is wanted but not committed; an Intention is internally committed; a Commitment is socially committed toward another agent. Desire and Intention are intrinsic modes inhering in one agent; a Commitment is a relator mediating at least two. * A Goal is the propositional content — a described state of affairs (gmeow:SocialObject), satisfied by situations via gmeow:satisfiedBy. DOLCE DnS arrives at the same shape independently (goal as a Description satisfied by Situations); the convergence is documented in docs.md. * gmeow:counterGoal is CONSTITUTIVE opposition — the named shadow that partly defines the goal. Strictly stronger than an antonym edge: the counter-goal is part of what the goal means, not merely its lexical opposite. * Whether a situation satisfies a goal is a vantage-indexed claim through the statement layer, never a global verdict (Principle 9). Whose goal it is, is indexed the same way: goals attributed to an agent by an observer and goals avowed by the agent are coexisting claims. * Flat-first, reify on demand (Principle 4): gmeow:hasGoal covers the 80% case; promote to Desire / Intention / Commitment when commitment grade, tenure, or standpoint matters; promote to gmeow:IntentionTenure (the StandpointTenure idiom) when adoption / revision of the intention is itself the fact of interest. Goals are revised by suppression, never deleted (Principle 10). * Goal decomposition, plan search, and means-end reasoning are solver-layer computations (Principle 12); the ontology records goals, their counter-goals, and who holds them. * Deontic force lives elsewhere: a Goal prescribes nothing. Norms that make conduct obligatory arrive with the norms extension (#351), which ranges gmeow:prescribedConduct over Goal — the dependency points extension → core, never back.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/teleology

docs.title: GMEOW Temporal Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Temporal Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/temporal CURIE: gmeow:slices/temporal

Type: owl:Ontology

Cross-cutting temporal facility (the OWL-Time superset layer): time intervals, instants, temporal reference frames, named periods, temporal measurements, and reified time-scoped relations, reused by every slice for facts that hold over a period (mailbox residence, address/role tenure, etc.). Lighter cases use the validFrom/validUntil RDF-star annotation properties.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/temporal

docs.title: GMEOW Trust Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Trust Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/trust CURIE: gmeow:slices/trust

Type: owl:Ontology

A cross-cutting trust facility: cryptographic keys, certifications (key↔identity attestations) and perspectival owner-trust — the Web-of-Trust superset layer (OpenPGP RFC 4880/9580, X.509, SSH, Nostr; aligned to the WOT schema). Reused wherever identity must be vouched for: contacts, accounts, and message signatures (the messaging-trust module builds on this). Trust here is asserted and perspectival; trust METRICS (transitive validity propagation) are deliberately left outside the logical core — represent inputs and outputs, never compute them in OWL.

STANDPOINT DOCTRINE (#51). The trust module exercises the three-axis separation that governs every contested-fact slice: gmeow:accordingTo (whose frame holds the claim true) ⟂ gmeow:wasAttributedTo (which source recorded it) ⟂ gmeow:confidence (how sure we are). A gmeow:TrustAssertion is already perspectival (its gmeow:trustor is the frame holder), but the underlying gmeow:Certification — a key↔identity binding — can ALSO be disputed across standpoints: one standpoint holds the binding unequivocal, another refutes it. The three axes never bridge (Principle 9); a neutral archive can record a partisan claim (source ≠ standpoint), and a claim can be high-confidence-that-S-holds-it yet about a frame we disagree with (confidence ≠ standpoint). There is NO trust-specific dispute mechanism, no primaryCertification, no preferredTrust — only the cross-cutting #43 facility.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/trust

docs.title: GMEOW Versions Module
docs.text:
The GMEOW Versions Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/versions CURIE: gmeow:slices/versions

Type: owl:Ontology

Cross-cutting version-set and version-membership facility for information-object lineages. Reuses the universal claim stack (Observation / Relator) so that version roles — canonical, variant, latest, stable, LTS, deprecated, yanked, etc. — are standpoint-scoped claims coexisting without privilege (Principle 9), never hard-coded as essential types. Suppressed versions remain first-class with gmeow:displayable false (Principle 10). Attestation evidence (signatures, SLSA, DOI assertions) belongs in #162 and composes with this layer; it is not embedded here.

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/versions

docs.title: according to
docs.text:
The standpoint / frame within which the annotated statement is asserted true — according to whom. DISTINCT from gmeow:wasAttributedTo (which source RECORDED the claim) and gmeow:confidence (how sure we are); a claim may carry all three with no inferential bridge among them. Its value is a gmeow:Agent (a polity, community, or organization IRI) or a gmeow:Standpoint individual (a frame that needs its own identity). When a statement is promoted to a reified gmeow:Observation, gmeow:accordingTo becomes the gmeow:vantage of the relator (vantage ⊑ accordingTo — documented, not axiomatised, because accordingTo is an AnnotationProperty and vantage is an ObjectProperty). Standpoint-TIME — when the frame held this position — rides gmeow:validFrom / gmeow:validUntil on the same statement in the light case, or a reified gmeow:StandpointTenure when the adoption / withdrawal is itself the fact of interest. The range is intentionally open. An unindexed statement is held according to gmeow:universalStandpoint (the uncontested global facts).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/accordingTo CURIE: gmeow:accordingTo

NOT functional, and deliberately so: the same diegetic event carries coexisting positions in a discourse frame and a story frame, and their disagreement is the flashback made queryable rather than a contradiction (Principle 9).

docs.title: coarsen guarded
docs.text:
Marks a property as PRECISION-BEARING for disclosure control (#282, CONSTITUTION P10): when a projection branch reads this property of a subject, the mapping compiler injects a guard so the subject's precise values never pass a gmeow:coarsenTo mark — the coarse form is published only by a profile's explicit coarsening branch. Ontology-derived, never a hand list: annotating a new precise-value property extends every generated projection's guards on the next regenerate.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/coarsenGuarded CURIE: gmeow:coarsenGuarded

annotation property

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/kernel

docs.title: coarsen to
docs.text:
Disclosure control: marks a value/relator so that at projection time it is generalized to no finer than the named gmeow:GranularityLevel — a coarser ancestor is emitted instead of the precise value (e.g. an enclosing city rather than exact coordinates), never by deletion. The generalization sibling of gmeow:displayable false (withhold); together they are the single 'withhold or coarsen under a trigger' mechanism of CONSTITUTION P10. Domain-free, like gmeow:displayable. The coarse value is obtained by walking gmeow:generalizesVia (default gmeow:partOf); any geometry/geomask computation stays in the solver layer (P12). When both apply, displayable false (withhold) wins over coarsen.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/coarsenTo CURIE: gmeow:coarsenTo

docs.text:

A new annotated axis receives Principle 9 enforcement by construction.

docs.text:
An observation that serves as a cue or indicator of deception in the event — a behavioural, linguistic, or evidential signal. Non-functional: a deception event may have many cues, and competing standpoint-indexed cue claims coexist (Principle 9). The scoring and weighting of cues is solver-layer (Principle 12).

docs.text:
An attributed, defeasible standpoint claim that the event was carried out with deceptive intent. The vantage is the assessor (who attributes the intent), not the deceiver; the claim carries gmeow:confidence and gmeow:wasAttributedTo. Intent is NEVER entailed by the reasoner — it is a contestable attribution that coexists with its denial (Principle 9).

docs.title: displayable
docs.text:
Whether a name or identity facet may be shown in interfaces and reports. The ONLY display control in the model — across naming (gmeow:Appellation) and identity (gmeow:IdentityFacet: gender/orientation), deliberately no preferred/primary marker (display selection is locale-relative and symmetric). It is intentionally domain-free so it applies to both. Superseded names (especially deadnames) and superseded gender/orientation labels set this false; consumers MUST honour false and never surface the string. NOT functional: in a multi-source merge, sources may disagree, and those claims must coexist rather than force a global inconsistency — the cautious value (false) wins at the projection layer. Cardinality is enforced by SHACL on data, not by the logical core.

docs.text:

docs.title: edition of
docs.text:

docs.text:
