docs.text:
Relates a value, entity, or claim to the projection consumers it is eligible for — the explicit who facet of disclosure control. Domain-free (universal, like hasGranularity and hasSensitivity). NOT functional: in a multi-source merge sources may state different consumer eligibilities, and those claims coexist rather than force the reasoner to collapse distinct consumers (Principle 9).

docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.title: emotion bearer
docs.text:
The agent in whom this emotion inheres. Functional and mandatory (SHACL): an intrinsic mode has exactly one bearer (the intentBearer pattern).

docs.text:
The kind(s) of this emotion. NOT functional: blended emotions carry several types, and classifications from different traditions coexist (Principle 9). At least one (SHACL); open vocabulary (sh:nodeKind sh:IRI, never sh:in).

docs.text:
The monetary compensation of an employment, expressed as a MonetaryAmount with explicit currency frame (Principle 11). Non-functional: a single employment may have several compensation figures over time (raises, bonuses, multi-currency arrangements), recorded as co-equal standpoint-indexed claims.

docs.title: employment interval
docs.text:
The time interval over which the employment holds. A relator carries its period this way (matching gmeow:participationInterval, gmeow:membershipInterval) rather than via gmeow:duringInterval, which is reserved for gufo:Situation-based time-scoped relations. Open-ended (no end instant) when the employment is current.

docs.title: employment occupation
docs.text:
The occupation associated with this employment, drawn from an open vocabulary such as ESCO or SOC. Functional: an employment maps to one canonical occupation; an agent with several occupations has several employment records.

docs.text:
The role borne by this employment — a job title, position, or function. Functional: an employment has one canonical role at a time; a change of role is a new employment record or a standpoint-indexed claim. Specializes gmeow:hasRole.

docs.title: employment seniority
docs.text:
The seniority level of an employment — one of the open gmeow:SeniorityLevel values. Functional: an employment has one canonical seniority at a time; a promotion is a new employment record or a standpoint-indexed claim. Orthogonal to employment type and role.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/employmentSeniority CURIE: gmeow:employmentSeniority

object property · domain gmeow:Employment · range gmeow:SeniorityLevel · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/employment

docs.title: employment type
docs.text:
The kind of employment — one of the open gmeow:EmploymentType values. Functional: an employment has one canonical type at a time; a change of type is a new employment record or a standpoint-indexed claim.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/employmentType CURIE: gmeow:employmentType

object property · domain gmeow:Employment · range gmeow:EmploymentType · functional

docs.title: endorses
docs.text:
A convenience shortcut recording that one agent vouches for another. Deliberately NOT symmetric (endorsement is directional) and NOT transitive (trust must not propagate inside the reasoner — that is the metric the perspectival TrustAssertion bounds). Use gmeow:TrustAssertion for leveled, dated, perspectival trust.

docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.text:
The origin of a movement event — where a migration, move, journey, or relocation departed from. A specialisation of gmeow:eventLocation (the origin IS a location of the event), so plain location consumers still see it. Pairs with gmeow:eventToLocation; the endpoint pair is the discrete sibling of the continuous gmeow:eventTrajectory (schema:MoveAction's fromLocation).

docs.text:
The crisp, known time interval over which an event occurred (reuses the temporal module's gmeow:TimeInterval). For a point-like occurrence use gmeow:eventTime; for an approximate date use gmeow:earliestStart / gmeow:latestEnd + gmeow:temporalPrecision.

docs.text:
A location at which an event occurred — a geographic gmeow:Place, a gmeow:VirtualLocation, or any other gmeow:Location (the full superset). Non-functional: an event may span several locations, and competing standpoint-indexed locations coexist.

docs.text:
An observation made during or about an event. Inverse of gmeow:observationEvent (observations module). Non-functional: an event may have many observations, and competing standpoint-indexed observations coexist (Principle 9).

docs.text:
A spacetime slice of an event, expressed as a gmeow:LocationState that carries location, time interval or instant, pose, and optional velocity relative to an explicit reference frame (Principle 11). Reuses LocationState rather than minting a parallel 4D class. Multiple slices may coexist for the same event.

docs.text:
The instant at which a point-like event occurred (xsd:dateTime — DL-clean, never xsd:date). Replaces the former free-text gmeow:eventDate. Non-functional: competing standpoint-indexed dates coexist as confidence-weighted statements.

docs.text:
The destination of a movement event — where a migration, move, journey, or relocation arrived. A specialisation of gmeow:eventLocation, pairing with gmeow:eventFromLocation (schema:MoveAction's toLocation).

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/events

docs.text:
The trajectory of a moving event — a parade, march, migration, or procession — describing its continuous space-time path. Reuses the gmeow:Trajectory facility from the locations module (#94). Non-functional: competing trajectory claims from different sources coexist (Principle 9).

docs.text:
The kind(s) of an event, drawn from the open gmeow:EventType value vocabulary. Non-functional: an occurrence may carry several types (a wedding that is also a religious rite), and competing standpoint-indexed type claims coexist rather than contradict.

The original date/time of the occurrence being excepted — the instance that would have been generated by the recurrence rule.

The replacement event for a rescheduled occurrence. Absent for a pure cancellation.

The event schedule to which this exception applies.

docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.text:
Relates an Execution to the specific ProcedureStep it enacts. Non-functional: an execution may enact multiple steps (a batch run), and competing enactment claims coexist.

docs.text:
An agent that took part in an execution — the flat 80%-case shortcut. Non-functional. Promote to a gmeow:Participation node when the role, period, confidence, or evidence of the participation must be recorded.

docs.text:
The status of an execution occurrence, drawn from the open gmeow:ExecutionStatus value vocabulary. Non-functional: competing assessments from different monitoring sources coexist (Principle 9).

docs.text:
The exemplar's direction. Functional and mandatory (SHACL): an exemplar that cannot say whether to emulate or avoid is just a citation.

Range intentionally open. NOT functional, optional: span-pinned exemplars need no subject, and subject + selector may coexist (the span shows one instance of the pattern; the subject names its bearer). docs.title: GTS head id
docs.text:
The chain head of a segment — the content-id of its last frame, written 'blake3:'. Transitively commits to the segment's entire history (spec §9.1), making it a version fingerprint of the segment rather than a digest of its bytes: hence a subproperty of gmeow:versionFingerprint, distinct from gmeow:contentDigest (which is byte-exact identity and applies to the file or a blob as a whole). Functional: a segment has exactly one head.

docs.text:

The value is the blob digest string; the docs-in-sync invariant (every guide anchor resolves to a live term) is enforced by the package build, so the linkage is trustworthy from the hash chain alone (Principle 7).

docs.title: has aboutness
docs.text:
Relates an information carrier (a document, span, segment, citation act, exemplar, or statement via the statement layer) to its aboutness mode — the explicit facet recording whether the carrier describes its subject or enacts it. Domain-free (universal, like hasGranularity, hasDeterminacy, and hasSensitivity). NOT functional: a carrier may bear different aboutness modes toward different subjects, and in a multi-vantage setting classifications coexist rather than force the reasoner to collapse them (Principle 9). An owl:AnnotationProperty (unlike the other three axes' ObjectProperties) because aboutness is routinely asserted ABOUT statements through the statement layer, where the annotation form keeps the generated OWL downcast in OWL 2 DL — the gmeow:accordingTo pattern (Principle 3). The subject toward which the mode holds is carried by the surrounding construct (the citation's cited entity, the exemplar's criterion, the statement cell) — never inferred.

object property · domain gmeow:Place · range gmeow:Geometry

docs.text:

docs.text:

A form of ADDRESS, sex/gender-independent — MUST NOT be inferred from gender identity/expression, sex-assigned-at-birth or orientation.

docs.text:

object property · domain gmeow:Project · range gmeow:Repository

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/software

docs.title: has rights statement

docs.text:

docs.text:
The SLSA supply-chain integrity level (1–4) asserted by an attestation. Non-functional: competing assessments from different verifiers coexist (Principle 9).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSLSALevel CURIE: gmeow:hasSLSALevel

object property · domain gmeow:Attestation · range gmeow:SLSALevel

docs.text:

object property · domain gmeow:Criterion · range gmeow:ScoreAnchor

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/norms

docs.title: has segment
docs.text:
Relates a whole (work, release, installment, or another segment) to a structural part. Non-functional: a work may have many segments. Inverse of gmeow:segmentOf.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSegment CURIE: gmeow:hasSegment

object property · range gmeow:ContentSegment

Sub-property of: gmeow:hasPart

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/documents

docs.title: has sensitivity
docs.text:
Relates a value, entity, or claim to its privacy-sensitivity level — the explicit facet that drives disclosure-control decisions (coarsenTo / displayable) at projection time under a consent guard. Domain-free (universal, like hasGranularity and hasDeterminacy). NOT functional: in a multi-source merge sources may state different sensitivity levels, and those claims coexist rather than force the reasoner to collapse distinct levels. Distinct from gmeow:confidence (epistemic certainty) and from gmeow:hasDeterminacy (ontic model).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSensitivity CURIE: gmeow:hasSensitivity

object property · range gmeow:SensitivityLevel

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/kernel

docs.title: has sensory observation
docs.text:
Links an entity to a sensory observation that measured one of its properties. Non-functional: multiple sensors may observe the same property of the same entity, and those readings coexist without collapse (Principle 9).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSensoryObservation CURIE: gmeow:hasSensoryObservation

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:SensoryObservation

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/sensory

docs.title: has sensory quantity
docs.text:
Flat shortcut linking an entity to the scalar quantity result of a sensory observation of its property. Derived via property chain from the reified observation path (hasSensoryObservation ∘ sensoryResult). Non-simple: kept out of cardinality axioms.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSensoryQuantity CURIE: gmeow:hasSensoryQuantity

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:SensoryQuantity

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/sensory

docs.title: has sequence coordinates
docs.text:

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSequenceCoordinates CURIE: gmeow:hasSequenceCoordinates

object property · domain gmeow:SequenceFeature · range gmeow:SequenceCoordinates

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: has sequence feature
docs.text:
Links a biological sequence location to a feature annotation on that sequence. Non-functional: a single location may carry multiple features (overlapping genes, nested exons, multiple SNPs).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSequenceFeature CURIE: gmeow:hasSequenceFeature

object property · domain gmeow:BiologicalSequenceLocation · range gmeow:SequenceFeature

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: has sexual orientation
docs.text:
Relates a person to a self-asserted sexual-orientation facet. Non-functional and contextual; a superseded one is kept with gmeow:displayable false, never deleted. MUST NOT be inferred from gmeow:hasRomanticOrientation, gmeow:hasGenderIdentity, gmeow:sexAssignedAtBirth, pronouns or honorifics.

object property · domain gmeow:Person · range gmeow:SexualOrientation

docs.text:

object property · domain gmeow:Person · range gmeow:Person

Sub-property of: gmeow:connectsTo

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/genealogy

docs.title: has signature
docs.text:
Relates an entity, attestation, or artifact to a cryptographic signature over it. Domain-free (universal spine): anything may carry a signature. The message-specific convenience property with domain gmeow:Message lives in the messaging-trust module as a historical subproperty.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSignature CURIE: gmeow:hasSignature

object property · range gmeow:CryptographicSignature

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/attestation

docs.title: has site
docs.text:
Relates an organization to a location it occupies or operates from — a headquarters, branch, or registered office. Reuses the places module's gmeow:Location. Non-functional: an organization may have several sites, and competing standpoint-indexed location claims coexist.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSite CURIE: gmeow:hasSite

object property · domain gmeow:Organization · range gmeow:Location

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/organization

docs.title: has skill
docs.text:
Relates an agent to a skill it possesses. Non-functional — an agent may have many skills. The leveled, scaled detail is carried by the reified gmeow:SkillProficiency.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSkill CURIE: gmeow:hasSkill

object property · domain gmeow:Agent · range gmeow:Skill

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/expertise

docs.title: has software name
docs.text:
Relates a project or product to a structured gmeow:SoftwareName it bears; the software-scoped specialization of gmeow:hasAppellation. Non-functional — a project may bear many co-equal names; none is primary.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSoftwareName CURIE: gmeow:hasSoftwareName

object property · range gmeow:SoftwareName

Sub-property of: gmeow:hasAppellation

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/software

docs.title: has spatial measurement
docs.text:
Links an entity to a spatial measurement describing its coordinates, geometry, pose, or spatial extent. Flat form for the common case; promote to full reified SpatialMeasurement when vantage, confidence, temporal scope, or standpoint matter.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSpatialMeasurement CURIE: gmeow:hasSpatialMeasurement

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:SpatialMeasurement

docs.title: has spouse
docs.text:
Relates a person to a spouse; symmetric.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSpouse CURIE: gmeow:hasSpouse

object property · domain gmeow:Person · range gmeow:Person

Sub-property of: gmeow:connectsTo

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/genealogy

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasStartInstant CURIE: gmeow:hasStartInstant

object property · domain gmeow:TimeInterval · range gmeow:Instant · functional

docs.text:
Links an entity to a stream of observations or samples about it. Non-functional: an entity may have multiple co-existing streams from different platforms or sensors (Principle 9), and no stream is privileged.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasStream CURIE: gmeow:hasStream

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:Stream

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/observations

docs.text:
Relates an event to a constituent sub-event; the transitive inverse of gmeow:subEventOf.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSubEvent CURIE: gmeow:hasSubEvent

object property · domain gmeow:Event · range gmeow:Event

Sub-property of: gmeow:hasPart

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/events

docs.text:
Relates a Procedure to a constituent subprocess Procedure; the transitive inverse of gmeow:subProcedureOf.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasSubProcedure CURIE: gmeow:hasSubProcedure

object property · domain gmeow:Procedure · range gmeow:Procedure

docs.title: has tag
docs.text:
Relates an entity to a user-minted tag — the 80% flat shortcut. Non-functional: an entity may carry many co-equal tags. Period, confidence, tagger and suppression are carried via RDF-star statement annotations (gmeow:validFrom, gmeow:validUntil, gmeow:confidence, gmeow:displayable) on the shortcut; promote to a gmeow:Tagging relator when the act itself must be a node.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasTag CURIE: gmeow:hasTag

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:Tag

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/tags

docs.title: has temporal frame
docs.text:
Relates a time interval to the temporal frame in which its bounds are expressed.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasTemporalFrame CURIE: gmeow:hasTemporalFrame

object property · domain gmeow:TimeInterval · range gmeow:TemporalFrame

Sub-property of: gmeow:hasReferenceFrame

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/temporal

docs.title: has temporal measurement
docs.text:
Relates an entity (event, artifact, place, sample) to a temporal measurement assigned to it.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasTemporalMeasurement CURIE: gmeow:hasTemporalMeasurement

object property · range gmeow:TemporalMeasurement

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/temporal

docs.title: has time scale
docs.text:
The time standard associated with a celestial reference frame. Functional: a frame uses exactly one time scale.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasTimeScale CURIE: gmeow:hasTimeScale

object property · domain gmeow:ReferenceFrame · range gmeow:TimeScale · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: has title
docs.text:
Relates a creative work to a structured gmeow:CreativeWorkTitle it bears; the creative-work-scoped specialization of gmeow:hasAppellation. Non-functional — a work bears many co-equal titles (original, translated, transliterated, regional); none is primary, and superseded ones set gmeow:displayable false. The structured replacement for the flat gmeow:title literal when multilingual or statement-level metadata is needed.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasTitle CURIE: gmeow:hasTitle

object property · domain gmeow:CreativeWork · range gmeow:CreativeWorkTitle

Sub-property of: gmeow:hasAppellation

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/documents

docs.title: has trademark
docs.text:
Relates an entity (a mark, product or organization) to a trademark right over it.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasTrademark CURIE: gmeow:hasTrademark

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:Trademark

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/rights

docs.title: has trajectory sample
docs.text:
A discrete location-state sample composing this trajectory. Non-functional: a trajectory typically has many samples, and multiple sampling strategies (e.g. GPS every second vs. radar every minute) may coexist for the same trajectory (Principle 9).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasTrajectorySample CURIE: gmeow:hasTrajectorySample

object property · domain gmeow:Trajectory · range gmeow:LocationState

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: has translator
docs.text:
Relates a creative work to an agent that translated it into another language or notation. A flat shortcut subproperty of gmeow:hasContributor.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasTranslator CURIE: gmeow:hasTranslator

object property · domain gmeow:CreativeWork · range gmeow:Agent

Sub-property of: gmeow:hasContributor

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/creative-works

docs.title: has tuning frame
docs.text:
The tuning system relative to which this pitch value or interval is expressed. Non-functional globally so that higher-level musical entities may carry multiple coexisting tuning frames (e.g., a detuned guitar over a 12-EDO synth); each PitchValue/PitchInterval is constrained to exactly one frame by SHACL (Principle 11).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasTuningFrame CURIE: gmeow:hasTuningFrame

object property · domain gmeow:PitchExpression · range gmeow:TuningSystem

Sub-property of: gmeow:hasReferenceFrame

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/music

docs.title: has unit
docs.text:
Relates a quantitative value or measurement to its QUDT unit (by reference, never imported). Domain-free: used by temporal measurements, spatial measurements, and any other quantified claim.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasUnit CURIE: gmeow:hasUnit

object property · range qudt:Unit · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/kernel

docs.title: has used
docs.text:
Records that an agent has used some entity (a tool, service, or work). The period is carried with gmeow:validFrom/validUntil on the statement.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasUsed CURIE: gmeow:hasUsed

object property · domain gmeow:Agent · range gmeow:Entity

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/contacts

docs.title: has utilization
docs.text:
Links a location to a utilization measurement describing the ratio of occupancy to capacity. Flat form for the common case; promote to full reified Utilization when vantage, confidence, temporal scope, or standpoint matter.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasUtilization CURIE: gmeow:hasUtilization

object property · domain gmeow:Location · range gmeow:Utilization

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: has verification status
docs.text:
The categorical outcome of a verification result. Non-functional: a single result may carry multiple status interpretations (e.g. 'verified but expired').

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasVerificationStatus CURIE: gmeow:hasVerificationStatus

object property · domain gmeow:VerificationResult · range gmeow:VerificationStatus

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/attestation

docs.title: has version
docs.text:
A related resource that is a version, edition, or adaptation of the described resource. Inverse of gmeow:versionOf.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasVersion CURIE: gmeow:hasVersion

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:Entity

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/creative-works

docs.title: has web page
docs.text:
Relates an entity to a web page representing it — a homepage, a profile page, a project site. The structured form of a 'website / URL' field: the page is a first-class gmeow:WebPage (documents module) whose IRI is its URL, so it can itself carry a title, language, and rights. Non-functional — an entity may have several pages.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasWebPage CURIE: gmeow:hasWebPage

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:WebPage

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/entities

docs.title: has wikilink
docs.text:
A directed wikilink edge projected from mentions or relatedNote for Markdown / PKM round-trip. Not asserted in the canonical graph; materialized by the markdown projection (queries/projections/markdown.rq).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasWikilink CURIE: gmeow:hasWikilink

object property · domain gmeow:Note · range gmeow:Note

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/notes

docs.title: has worked with
docs.text:
Records that two agents have worked together; symmetric. The period is carried with gmeow:validFrom/validUntil on the statement, or reified as a gmeow:ProfessionalRelationship.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hasWorkedWith CURIE: gmeow:hasWorkedWith

object property · domain gmeow:Agent · range gmeow:Agent

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/contacts

docs.title: hazard bearer
docs.text:
The entity in which this hazard inheres. Functional and mandatory (SHACL): a disposition has exactly one bearer (gUFO inherence, asserted with GMEOW's own property — Principle 5). The same danger borne by two systems is two hazards.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hazardBearer CURIE: gmeow:hazardBearer

object property · domain gmeow:Hazard · range gmeow:Entity · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/risk

docs.title: hazard severity
docs.text:
The hazard's graded severity, when graded standalone (a hazard feeding a cascade usually inherits attention from the cascade's grade). NOT functional (PR #385 review — evaluative, source-variable; the hasAuthorityLevel convention); optional, at most one per base graph (SHACL).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/hazardSeverity CURIE: gmeow:hazardSeverity

object property · domain gmeow:Hazard · range gmeow:SeverityLevel

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/risk

docs.title: header name
docs.text:
The field name of a message header.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/headerName CURIE: gmeow:headerName

datatype property · domain gmeow:MessageHeader · range rdfs:Literal · functional

datatype property · domain gmeow:MessageHeader · range rdfs:Literal · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/email

docs.title: heading
docs.text:
The compass direction an entity is facing, typically clockwise from north, in degrees.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/heading CURIE: gmeow:heading

datatype property · domain gmeow:Orientation · range xsd:double

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: held standpoint
docs.text:
The standpoint claim that the deceiver actually holds to be true — the private belief or position that contrasts with the projected standpoint in a deception event. Non-functional: a complex deception may involve multiple held standpoints.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/heldStandpoint CURIE: gmeow:heldStandpoint

object property · domain gmeow:Event · range gmeow:StandpointClaim

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/deception

docs.title: holding agent
docs.text:
The agent that holds the asset. Functional: a holding is held by exactly one agent.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/holdingAgent CURIE: gmeow:holdingAgent

object property · domain gmeow:Holding · range gmeow:Agent · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/finance

docs.title: holding asset
docs.text:
The financial asset that is held. Functional: a holding is of exactly one asset.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/holdingAsset CURIE: gmeow:holdingAsset

object property · domain gmeow:Holding · range gmeow:Asset · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/finance

docs.title: holding cost basis
docs.text:
The cost basis of the holding — the original monetary amount paid to acquire the asset. Functional: a holding has one canonical cost basis (disputed values are standpoint-indexed claims).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/holdingCostBasis CURIE: gmeow:holdingCostBasis

object property · domain gmeow:Holding · range gmeow:MonetaryAmount · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/finance

When the host ceases to exist, the hosted frame deactivates (destruction event or existenceInterval end). Non-functional: contested authorship or multi-agent shared frames may have multiple host claims that coexist (Principle 9).

docs.title: name
docs.text:
A simple label by which an entity is known — the rdfs:label tier, for entities that do not need the full naming apparatus (organizations, software agents, sources, keys). Persons' names are modelled as gmeow:PersonName (names module); a flat given/family ('First Last') rendering is produced by downcasting that structured model in the projection layer, not stored here. Carries no precedence over an entity's other names. Language-tag the literal where applicable.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/name CURIE: gmeow:name

docs.title: name language
docs.text:
The first-class gmeow:Language an appellation's surface form is in. Language is ALWAYS a first-class gmeow:Language (registry-INDEPENDENT, self-minted IRI) — never a bare BCP-47 literal; codes (e.g. "ja", "zh") live on the Language via gmeow:languageCode, so a code-less conlang or AI-minted language names co-equally. FUNCTIONAL — exactly one language per appellation: co-equal multilingual names are modelled as SEPARATE co-equal gmeow:Appellation instances (one per language), never by multi-tagging a single name (that is what keeps naming anti-colonial and symmetric). Drives locale-relative, symmetric display selection — never a ranking of one name above another. The script the form is written in is gmeow:nameScript (bridging to a first-class gmeow:WritingSystem).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/nameLanguage CURIE: gmeow:nameLanguage

docs.title: naming note
docs.text:
An explicit justification for a term local name that the primary/preferred/default/main naming lint (CONSTITUTION P9, #281) would otherwise reject. Legitimate value-vocabulary uses exist — gmeow:scriptRolePrimary names a linguistic reality (one co-equal value among seven), gmeow:sourceTierPrimary is the standard bibliographic axis — and this annotation records that judgment so the lint enforces it instead of relying on audit-time discretion. A term carrying namingNote must still never be a selector that privileges one co-equal claim over another.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/namingNote CURIE: gmeow:namingNote

docs.title: narrated in
docs.text:
Flat 80% seam link, content-side orientation: the diegetic entity or event appears in the segment. The projection-friendly direction — Wikidata P1441 'present in work' is exactly this edge (SSSOM row deferred to the alignment window). Domain intentionally open. The place over which this regulatory overlay applies. Functional: an overlay concerns exactly one place (constitutive of the situation's identity). The place carries the geographic geometry; the overlay carries the regulation and temporal scope.

docs.text:

docs.title: overrides
docs.text:
Pairwise defeasible precedence: when both norms apply, the subject prevails over the object — according to whoever asserts this claim (statement-layer indexed like everything else). DELIBERATELY NOT TRANSITIVE: lex-superior chains, specificity reasoning, and cycle handling are solver inferences over the recorded pairs, never reasoner entailments (Principle 12). Irreflexive by SHACL. The flat 80% case; promote to gmeow:PrecedenceTenure when the precedence held over an interval is itself the fact of interest.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/overrides CURIE: gmeow:overrides

A functional specialisation of gmeow:isAbout (a page has at most one principal subject, though it may mention many). When the principal subject is an Agent the page is inferred a gmeow:ProfilePage.

docs.title: pairs with
docs.text:
Links the two halves of a flat-first/reify-on-demand pair — the flat shortcut and the reified relator that carries the same relationship when period, role, confidence, or standpoint must be first-class (gmeow:hasGoal ↔ gmeow:IntentionTenure; gmeow:hasLicense ↔ gmeow:License; gmeow:narrates ↔ gmeow:NarrationUsage). Symmetric by doctrine, asserted in one direction (flat → reified) and read both ways by tooling; an AnnotationProperty so the pairing is machine-usable documentation (gmeow describe renders the promotion path from it), never a logical bridge (Principle 12: no axiom makes the flat form entail the relator).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/pairsWith CURIE: gmeow:pairsWith

docs.title: prescribed conduct
docs.text:
The conduct the norm is about — an event type, a goal (#350), a situation, or a rights action (via the #352 graft). The range is intentionally open (the tenurePosition precedent): asserting a closed range union would either dangle across module boundaries or vanish from the generated schema surface, and the graft would force dual-typing of the RightsAction vocabulary. NOT functional: one norm may govern several conducts jointly.

docs.title: proximity
docs.text:
Links an entity to a proximity measurement describing its distance or dissimilarity to another entity. The measurement carries the scalar value (via observationResult → ScalarQuantity), the reference frame (via hasReferenceFrame), and the target entity (via proximityTo). Flat form for the common case; promote to full reified Measurement when vantage, confidence, temporal scope, or standpoint matter.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/proximity CURIE: gmeow:proximity

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.text:

A Latin-script transliteration of THIS SAME appellation in another script (e.g. "Yamada Tarō" for "山田太郎"; pinyin for a Chinese name). Strictly a transliteration of one name — it NEVER bridges two distinct co-equal names (a Mandarin name is not the romanization of a Latin one).

docs.text:

Functional: one cell, one state — a blended reading at one position is several samples sharing a vantage. The claimModality axiom pattern applies: this plays the observationResult role without the subproperty (QualityValue ⟂ Entity).

docs.text:

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/scriptCode CURIE: gmeow:scriptCode

docs.text:

docs.text:
The interval over which a writing-system-usage held — e.g. Turkish-in-Arabic-script until 1928. A relator carries its period this way (matching names' NameUsage); lighter cases use gmeow:validFrom/validUntil on the statement. (Distinct from the names module's gmeow:usageInterval, which scopes a NameUsage.)

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/scriptUsageInterval CURIE: gmeow:scriptUsageInterval

Also usable as a statement-level annotation (RDF 1.2 / OWL axiom) to mark a quoted claim as self-asserted. Non-functional: a multi-source merge may carry both a self-assertion and a third-party record, which coexist rather than force a contradiction.

Non-functional: a work may source several frames, and a frame may have many sources. The specific role (source, witness, revision, adaptation) is carried by gmeow:accordingTo on the claim or by a reified relator when needed.

docs.title: source modified at
docs.text:
The last-modification time of the source artifact itself (e.g. a file mtime). A terminus-ante-quem on the recording of the claims this source carries — NOT valid-time (tenure) and NOT observation-time. Advisory and resettable; the reliable identity is gmeow:contentDigest. NOT functional: because a source is identified by its content digest, copies/syncs of the same bytes may legitimately report different modification times, which must coexist rather than force an inconsistency.

Distinct from gmeow:adjacentTo (RCC-8 EC: touching but not necessarily traversable) and from gmeow:containedInLocation (mereological containment).

The bridge to the SPDX / SBOM world (spdx:licenseId); the SPDX List also assigns each id a stable IRI under http://spdx.org/licenses/. docs.title: standpoint modality
docs.text:
The belief value a standpoint assigns the annotated proposition — how the standpoint holds it, not merely that it holds it. This single axis is at least as expressive as BOTH the Standpoint-Logic modal operators (□_S / ◊_S) AND the CRMinf belief value (true / false / probable / possible): gmeow:unequivocal (□, settled true), gmeow:probable (likely true), gmeow:conceivable (◊, possible), gmeow:refuted (□¬, settled false — the standpoint DENIES the proposition), gmeow:bullshit (indifference to truth — Frankfurt). Optional; ABSENT is read as unequivocal. Orthogonal to gmeow:confidence (our certainty about the standpoint's stance) and gmeow:accordingTo (whose frame). Refutation is what lets GMEOW distinguish a standpoint's explicit denial from its silence — the neutral-stance ambiguity flat models cannot resolve.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/standpointModality CURIE: gmeow:standpointModality

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/standpoint

docs.title: stream sample
docs.text:
Links a stream to an individual observation, location state, or other entity composing it. Non-functional: a stream typically has many samples, and multiple sampling strategies may coexist for the same stream (Principle 9). Ordering is implicit via sample timestamps, not asserted list structure (Principle 12).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/streamSample CURIE: gmeow:streamSample

object property · domain gmeow:Stream · range gmeow:Entity

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/observations

docs.title: stream sensor
docs.text:
The specific sensor or agent producing the stream. Non-functional: multiple sensors may contribute to one stream, and competing sensor claims coexist (Principle 9).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/streamSensor CURIE: gmeow:streamSensor

object property · domain gmeow:Stream · range gmeow:Agent

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/observations

docs.title: street address
docs.text:
The street-address coordinate value of a postal address, expressed along the gmeow:axisStreetAddress axis of the postal reference frame.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/streetAddress CURIE: gmeow:streetAddress

datatype property · domain gmeow:PostalAddress · range rdfs:Literal

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/contacts

docs.title: stronger than
docs.text:
Orders authority levels: the subject level carries more claimed authority than the object level. Transitive ON LEVELS ONLY (the gmeow:coarserThan pattern) — norms themselves are ordered by pairwise gmeow:overrides claims, never transitively.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/strongerThan CURIE: gmeow:strongerThan

object property · domain gmeow:AuthorityLevel · range gmeow:AuthorityLevel

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/norms

docs.title: style guide for
docs.text:

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/styleGuideFor CURIE: gmeow:styleGuideFor

object property · domain gmeow:StyleGuide

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/norms

docs.title: sub-event of
docs.text:
Relates an event to a larger event it is part of — a talk within a session within a conference. Transitive: a part of a part is a part (CIDOC-CRM P9 consists of). A specialization of the universal gmeow:partOf spine. Non-simple, so kept out of all cardinality axioms.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/subEventOf CURIE: gmeow:subEventOf

object property · domain gmeow:Event · range gmeow:Event

Sub-property of: gmeow:partOf

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/events

docs.title: sub-organization of
docs.text:
Relates an organization to a larger organization it is part of — a department or division within a company, a team within a department. Transitive (a team is part of the company through its division). A specialization of the universal gmeow:partOf spine. A department is thus a first-class gmeow:Organization, and a gmeow:Membership may target it directly. The 'department' field is the sub-organization a person's membership is in.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/subOrganizationOf CURIE: gmeow:subOrganizationOf

object property · domain gmeow:Organization · range gmeow:Organization

Sub-property of: gmeow:partOf

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/organization

docs.title: sub-procedure of
docs.text:
Relates a Procedure to a larger Procedure it is part of — subprocess composition. Transitive: a part of a part is a part. Specialisation of the universal gmeow:partOf spine. Non-simple, so kept out of all cardinality axioms.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/subProcedureOf CURIE: gmeow:subProcedureOf

object property · domain gmeow:Procedure · range gmeow:Procedure

Sub-property of: gmeow:partOf

docs.text:
A prefix stripped from a message subject during normalization (e.g. 'Re:', 'Fwd:', 'AW:'). A single message may have multiple nested prefixes, so this property is not functional.

docs.text:
An organization that begins or results from a multi-organization change event. Non-functional: a split has several successors, and competing standpoint-indexed successor claims coexist.

The community this summary condenses.

docs.title: superseded by
docs.text:
Links an entity to the entity that replaced it — Constantinople supersededBy Istanbul, the Soviet Union supersededBy the Russian Federation, a deprecated software release supersededBy its successor. Directional, NOT symmetric. The superseded entity is retained (never deleted) and may carry gmeow:displayable false.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/supersededBy CURIE: gmeow:supersededBy

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:Entity

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/lifecycle

docs.title: supersedes
docs.text:
Relates a newer entity, version, record, or claim-bearing artifact to a prior one it supersedes. Non-functional: one successor may consolidate several predecessors. Superseded entities remain first-class and usable; suppression from display is handled separately with gmeow:displayable false when appropriate.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/supersedes CURIE: gmeow:supersedes

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:Entity

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/coreference

docs.text:
Whether this evidence span supports, refutes, or is neutral toward the claim it grounds — the NLI/AIS verdict as data, orthogonal to the citations slice's gmeow:citationIntent (which classifies a CitationAct between works, not a span-to-claim stance). A refuting span never deletes the claim; it feeds a gmeow:Contradiction and the audit queries (P9, P10).

docs.text:
Whether this citation is asserted to support notability (encyclopedic significance) as distinct from factual verification. A citation may verify a fact (high evidential warrant) without supporting notability (e.g. a primary legal filing or a routine listing). Non-functional: competing notability assessments from different standpoints coexist (Principle 9).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/supportsNotability CURIE: gmeow:supportsNotability

datatype property · domain gmeow:CitationAct · range xsd:boolean

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/evidence

docs.title: symbolic system kind
docs.text:
The kind(s) of a symbolic system (gmeow:SymbolicSystemKind values). Non-functional — a system may serve multiple domains simultaneously.

docs.text:

docs.title: tag in scheme

docs.text:

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/tags

docs.title: tagging tag
docs.text:

object property · domain gmeow:Tagging · range gmeow:Tag · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/tags

object property · domain gmeow:Tagging · range gmeow:Entity · functional

docs.text:

Whether this recurring task continues until marked done, rather than stopping at a fixed count or end date.

object property · domain gmeow:Task · range gmeow:TaskStatus

datatype property · domain gmeow:Agent · range rdfs:Literal

docs.title: tenure agent
docs.text:
The agent whose intentional mode an intention-tenure records. Functional: one tenure, one agent.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/tenureAgent CURIE: gmeow:tenureAgent

object property · domain gmeow:IntentionTenure · range gmeow:Agent · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/teleology

docs.title: tenure determinacy
docs.text:
The ontic determinacy model of this land tenure's boundary or claim — crisp (surveyed), vague (approximate), fuzzy (probabilistic), or disputed. Non-functional: sources may disagree on determinacy, and those claims coexist.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/tenureDeterminacy CURIE: gmeow:tenureDeterminacy

object property · domain gmeow:LandTenure · range gmeow:Determinacy

Sub-property of: gmeow:hasDeterminacy

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: tenure intention
docs.text:
The desire or intention the tenure records the agent as holding over its interval. Functional: one tenure, one mode. Commitment tenure is carried by the Commitment relator's own temporal scope (relators are time-indexed by construction); the tenure class exists for the intrinsic modes, whose adoption and abandonment would otherwise be invisible.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/tenureIntention CURIE: gmeow:tenureIntention

docs.text:
The party (person, corporation, indigenous community, or other agent) that holds the rights recorded by this LandTenure. Functional: a single tenure has exactly one party. Joint ownership is modelled as multiple co-equal LandTenure instances, none privileged (Principle 9).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/tenureParty CURIE: gmeow:tenureParty

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: tenure place
docs.text:
The place (parcel, lot, or spatial unit) over which the rights of this LandTenure apply. Functional: a tenure concerns exactly one place (constitutive of the situation's identity).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/tenurePlace CURIE: gmeow:tenurePlace

object property · domain gmeow:LandTenure · range gmeow:Place · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: tenure position
docs.text:
The standpoint-indexed claim the tenure says the standpoint held over its interval — a reified statement (a gmeow:StatementMetadata cell in the statement DSL). The range is intentionally left open: the statement-DSL spec layer is not part of the reasoned import closure, so asserting it as rdfs:range would dangle in the merged graph. When a StandpointTenure generates a StandpointClaim observation, the tenurePosition becomes the observedFeature of the claim.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/tenurePosition CURIE: gmeow:tenurePosition

object property · domain gmeow:StandpointTenure

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/standpoint

docs.text:
The machine-readable rights statement (permissions, prohibitions, duties) that governs this land tenure. Links to the #21 rights facility by reference. Non-functional: multiple legal instruments may apply to the same tenure (e.g. national law + local ordinance + indigenous treaty).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/tenureRights CURIE: gmeow:tenureRights

object property · domain gmeow:LandTenure · range gmeow:RightsStatement

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.text:
The standpoint whose position a standpoint-tenure records. When a StandpointTenure generates a StandpointClaim observation, the tenureStandpoint becomes the vantage of the claim.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/tenureStandpoint CURIE: gmeow:tenureStandpoint

object property · domain gmeow:StandpointTenure · range gmeow:Standpoint · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/standpoint

docs.title: tenure type
docs.text:
The kind(s) of land tenure (a gmeow:LandTenureType individual). Non-functional: a single tenure may be classified by multiple sources as different types, and those claims coexist as evidence (Principle 9).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/tenureType CURIE: gmeow:tenureType

object property · domain gmeow:LandTenure · range gmeow:LandTenureType

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: tenured contact point
docs.text:
The contact point an address-tenure concerns.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/tenuredContactPoint CURIE: gmeow:tenuredContactPoint

object property · domain gmeow:AddressTenure · range gmeow:ContactPoint · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/contacts

docs.title: text direction
docs.text:
The writing direction(s) of a writing system (gmeow:TextDirection values). Non-functional — Japanese is both vertical-rtl and ltr.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/textDirection CURIE: gmeow:textDirection

docs.text:
The base subject of a conversation thread, with reply/forward prefixes stripped, used for display and grouping. Derived from the raw RFC 5322 Subject headers of the messages in the thread.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/threadSubject CURIE: gmeow:threadSubject

datatype property · domain gmeow:Thread · range rdfs:Literal

docs.title: time zone IANA id
docs.text:
The IANA time zone identifier, e.g. America/Toronto, Europe/Paris, UTC.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/timeZoneIanaId CURIE: gmeow:timeZoneIanaId

datatype property · domain gmeow:TimeZone · range xsd:string · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/calendar

docs.title: timezone
docs.text:
An IANA time-zone identifier for a location (e.g. "America/Edmonton"). Non-functional: a large place may span several zones.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/timezone CURIE: gmeow:timezone

datatype property · domain gmeow:Location · range rdfs:Literal

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: title
docs.text:
The title of a creative work.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/title CURIE: gmeow:title

datatype property · domain gmeow:CreativeWork · range rdfs:Literal

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/documents

docs.text:
A primary recipient address of a message (RFC 5322 To).

object property · domain gmeow:EmailMessage · range gmeow:EmailAddress

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/email

docs.title: tool arguments
docs.text:
The verbatim arguments payload presented to the tool (typically JSON), byte-faithful. For large payloads store a content digest literal instead ('blake3:…' — the gmeow:contentDigest convention): the digest is the value, resolvable from a content-addressed store. Functional: one arguments record per call.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/toolArguments CURIE: gmeow:toolArguments

docs.text:
The verbatim result payload the tool returned, byte-faithful — the PAYLOAD of the event, never a forward entity link: an entity the call produced links back via gmeow:wasGeneratedBy (Principle 5). For large payloads store a content digest literal instead ('blake3:…'), as gmeow:toolArguments. Functional: one result record per call.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/toolResult CURIE: gmeow:toolResult

datatype property · domain gmeow:ToolCall · range rdfs:Literal · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/agentic

docs.title: trademark holder
docs.text:
The agent that holds a trademark (the proprietor). A specialisation of gmeow:wasAttributedTo. Non-functional: a mark may be jointly held.

docs.text:

docs.title: trademark status
docs.text:
The status of a trademark — one of the gmeow:TrademarkStatus values (unregistered ™ / registered ® / pending / expired / cancelled). Functional.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/trademarkStatus CURIE: gmeow:trademarkStatus

object property · domain gmeow:Trademark · range gmeow:TrademarkStatus · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/rights

docs.title: trajectory of
docs.text:
The entity whose space-time path this trajectory describes. Functional: a trajectory belongs to exactly one entity.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/trajectoryOf CURIE: gmeow:trajectoryOf

docs.text:
The coordinate reference frame in which this trajectory's samples are expressed. Functional: a trajectory is expressed in exactly one frame; frame transformation is a solver concern (Principle 12).

docs.title: transaction amount
docs.text:
The monetary amount of a financial transaction, expressed as a MonetaryAmount. Functional: a single transaction occurrence has one canonical amount (disputed amounts are standpoint-indexed claims on separate statements, not additional values on the same transaction).

docs.title: transaction type
docs.text:

docs.text:
A flat shortcut asserting that a creative work is a transcription derived from another creative work. The reified form is a gmeow:CreativeDerivation with gmeow:derivationType gmeow:derivationTypeTranscription.

docs.title: vantage
docs.text:
The agent or standpoint from which the observation is made — the reified-object-property counterpart of gmeow:accordingTo. Semantically, gmeow:vantage ⊑ gmeow:accordingTo: when an annotated statement is promoted to a reified Observation, its gmeow:accordingTo becomes the gmeow:vantage of the relator. The agent in the vantage role — an observer, a sensor, a perceiver — IS a standpoint (Principle 9): no frame is privileged, and every vantage is a co-equal facet from which the claim is held. Range is gmeow:Entity (encompassing both gmeow:Agent and gmeow:Standpoint) because a vantage may be a bare agent (person, organization, software agent, sensor) or a gmeow:Standpoint individual when the frame needs its own identity. Non-functional: joint observations (a reading co-authored by two agencies) are valid.

datatype property · domain gmeow:VirtualLocation · range rdfs:Literal

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: wallet address
docs.text:
A public address of the crypto wallet. Non-functional: a single wallet may have multiple addresses (e.g. HD wallet derivation paths).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/walletAddress CURIE: gmeow:walletAddress

datatype property · domain gmeow:CryptoWallet · range rdfs:Literal

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/finance

docs.title: wallet key
docs.text:
The cryptographic key that controls the wallet. Non-functional: a wallet may be controlled by several keys (multi-sig) or the key may rotate over time.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/walletKey CURIE: gmeow:walletKey

object property · domain gmeow:CryptoWallet · range gmeow:CryptographicKey

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/finance

docs.title: wallet scheme
docs.text:
The blockchain scheme of the wallet — Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Monero, etc. Functional: a wallet operates on exactly one scheme (a multi-scheme container is several wallets).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/walletScheme CURIE: gmeow:walletScheme

object property · domain gmeow:CryptoWallet · range gmeow:WalletScheme · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/finance

docs.title: was associated with
docs.text:
Relates an activity to an agent associated with carrying it out — e.g. the software agent that ran an import. (Activity→Agent; the counterpart of gmeow:wasAttributedTo, which ascribes an endurant Entity to an agent.)

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/wasAssociatedWith CURIE: gmeow:wasAssociatedWith

object property · domain gmeow:Activity · range gmeow:Agent

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/provenance

docs.title: was attributed to
docs.text:
Ascribes responsibility for an entity to an agent.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/wasAttributedTo CURIE: gmeow:wasAttributedTo

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:Agent

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/provenance

docs.title: was derived from
docs.text:
Relates a derived thing to the thing it was derived from — e.g. a text extraction, summary, or embedding to its source; a commit to its parent commit; a trajectory to its sample stream. The derivation's confidence and generating agent are recorded with gmeow:confidence and gmeow:wasGeneratedBy. Domain-free so that events, endurants, and information objects may all participate in derivation chains.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/wasDerivedFrom CURIE: gmeow:wasDerivedFrom

object property

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/provenance

docs.title: was generated by
docs.text:
Relates an entity to the activity that produced it.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/wasGeneratedBy CURIE: gmeow:wasGeneratedBy

object property · domain gmeow:Entity · range gmeow:Activity

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/provenance

docs.title: web URL
docs.text:
The human-readable web URL of the repository (e.g. the GitHub project page).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/webUrl CURIE: gmeow:webUrl

datatype property · domain gmeow:Repository · range rdfs:Literal

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/software

docs.title: what3words
docs.text:
A what3words address — three words that identify a 3m×3m square on Earth (e.g. 'filled.county.limes').

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/what3words CURIE: gmeow:what3words

datatype property · domain gmeow:Geocode · range xsd:string · functional

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/places

docs.title: within family
docs.text:
Anchors a reified kinship relationship in the family group it belongs to — the structural seam GEDCOM exchange requires (a child's family, a marriage's family). Optional: kinship claims stand alone; the family anchor is added when the family-group structure is itself a documented fact (#34 phase 3 — consumers: the gedcom projection and the published genealogy profiles).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/withinFamily CURIE: gmeow:withinFamily

object property · domain gmeow:KinRelationship · range gmeow:Family

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/genealogy

docs.title: writing system as notation
docs.text:
When a writing system is also a notation system — e.g. Braille as a tactile notation, or a bespoke conlang script that doubles as a featural notation. NON-FUNCTIONAL: a writing system may be classified as a notation by some standpoints and not by others (Principle 9).

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/writingSystemAsNotation CURIE: gmeow:writingSystemAsNotation

object property · domain gmeow:WritingSystem · range gmeow:NotationSystem

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/notation

docs.title: writing system type
docs.text:
The structural kind(s) of a writing system (gmeow:WritingSystemType values). Non-functional — a script may be classified plurally.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/writingSystemType CURIE: gmeow:writingSystemType

object property · domain gmeow:WritingSystem · range gmeow:WritingSystemType

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/languages

docs.title: written in language
docs.text:
Relates an information object — an expression, a document, a source tree, an inscription reading — to a first-class gmeow:Language it is written in. The registry-independent replacement for flat inLanguage tags: the object is a Language IRI, never a code literal (codes are alignments via gmeow:languageCode). Non-functional: content mixes languages, and a codebase uses several.

IRI: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/writtenInLanguage CURIE: gmeow:writtenInLanguage

object property · domain gmeow:InformationObject · range gmeow:Language

Defined by: https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/language

docs.title: yaw
docs.text:
Rotation about the vertical (typically z) axis, in degrees or radians as indicated by the reference frame.

datatype property · domain gmeow:Orientation · range xsd:double

docs.title: Slices
docs.text:
GMEOW is composed of self-contained slices. Each slice's manifest is the sole source of its identity, tier, dependencies, and consumer.

Slice Tier Profiles Dependencies Consumer accessibility extension — kernel, places Accessibility facets over places and routes; the schema.org accessibility projection. accounts core — kernel Online accounts for the mail corpus, email delivery, and finance. affect extension narrative kernel, observations The lbox principia importer (EPIC #348: affect/aesthetic annotations) and the narrative arc samples (#361: sampleState draws on EmotionType by soft reference, never dependency). DELIBERATELY THIN (P15): growth requires a new consumer; the size budget and expansion bar are recorded in docs.md. agentic extension — ai, entities, kernel, provenance, sources, temporal Project Lillith's agentic mode (#390, P15): tool-call trajectories audited in the same provenance graph as the agent's claims. First live producer: the gmeow memory MCP triad records its own store/revise calls as ToolCall provenance. DELIBERATELY THIN: growth requires a new consumer; the size budget is recorded in docs.md. aggregation extension — observations, places Spatial aggregation (count, density, k-anonymity) in the solver layer over places. agreements core — kernel, names Licences-as-agreements (rights), employment terms, and calendar RSVPs. ai core — entities, evidence, kernel, observations, provenance The flagship (P14): the gmeow PyPI client's Memory store, the MCP store/recall/revise triad (#297), the hallucination-resistant KG pattern + gmeow audit (#55), the claim-extraction eval suite (#298), and Project Lillith via extensions/graphrag. archaeological-evidence extension — events, kernel, language, observations, places, temporal Inscription readings and find contexts; the languages stress corpus (#173). attestation core — events, kernel, observations, provenance, trust Signed-claim envelopes for trust, software releases (SLSA/Sigstore), and GTS COSE signing. calendar core — agreements, events, kernel, temporal Scheduling atop events: the mail corpus's invitations (#139), the >25%-usage floor (named in #287). citations core claims, memory documents, evidence, kernel The citation/credit dogfood (#211): CITATION.cff projection, slice manifests, scholarly credit. connectivity extension — kernel, places Network/route topology for places and the virtual-location realm. contacts core — accounts, agreements, kernel, observations, places, temporal The mail corpus's address book; email-address structure (core half of the email split). coreference core memory documents, kernel Authority links from every slice to Wikidata and registries (P5, never owl:sameAs). creative-works core — citations, coreference, documents, kernel The WEMI spine under documents, software products, citations, and the music slice (#306). deception core — attestation, events, kernel, observations Graph-native epistemics of the lie (P16: core by commitment); the claim layer's refutations. documents core — creative-works, kernel, names, observations, places, standpoint, tags Creative-works manifestations, the mail corpus attachments, depictions of any entity. email extension — accounts, contacts, documents, entities, events, kernel, temporal, trust The mail corpus (#141): the dogfooded message model over core contacts/accounts. employment extension — entities, kernel, observations, organization, temporal CV/employment claims over organization and agreements; the mail corpus's signatures. entities core — contacts, documents, kernel, language, names, places, trust Every slice describing people, organizations, or things; the mail corpus; the identity facets. events core memory documents, kernel, observations, places, provenance, temporal Participation and life events across slices; the calendar slice; provenance activities. evidence core claims, memory citations, kernel The claim spine's EvidenceSpan (#55); evidential warrant for citations and deception analyses. expertise core — entities, kernel, organization, temporal Cross-cutting proficiency claims (promoted core, #287): skills, credentials, language proficiency. finance extension — accounts, agreements, documents, events, kernel, observations, places, temporal, trust Accounts, transactions, REA double-entry over core MonetaryAmount; FIBO alignment. gender core — entities, kernel, names, observations, sexuality Identity facets on persons (P16: core by commitment); the 7-axis orthogonality matrix. genealogy extension — entities, kernel, observations Kin relationships for the family-history use of the mail corpus; GEDCOM alignment. graphrag extension — ai, entities, kernel, observations, provenance Project Lillith — a GraphRAG deployment whose corpus, embeddings, indexes, retrievals, and derived entity graph must be auditable provenance, not pipeline internals (P15). gts core — attestation, creative-works, kernel, provenance, versions Describing and dogfooding GTS transport artifacts: packages, segments, profiles, chain heads, opaque frames, codecs, and compaction lineage (#267, docs/GTS-SPEC.md). images extension — documents, kernel, observations, temporal High-fidelity depiction (regions, scene graphs) atop core MediaObject; the gmeow-image CLI (#326). kernel core — — Every slice: the gUFO-grounded kernel (Entity, Agent, InformationObject, base relations). language core — kernel, names Every language-tagged literal (x-gmeow-*); names' romanizations; software's languages (P16 slim core). languages extension — expertise, kernel, language, observations, provenance, temporal Rich sociolinguistics (proficiency, scripts, varieties, diachrony) extending the core language slim slice. lexicon extension — documents, kernel, language, observations, temporal Lexical items and attestations for the language family; archaeological readings. lifecycle core — coreference, events, kernel, temporal Birth/death and existence events for persons and places across the corpus. music extension music creative-works, documents, events, kernel, language, observations, places, provenance, standpoint, temporal, versions The GTS music-package single-file format, the MCP analysis-claims surface, and the 19-case stress corpus that closes the #306 Music EPIC. names core memory agreements, contacts, entities, events, kernel, language, observations, places, temporal Every named entity (P9 anti-colonial naming); the mail corpus; display-safety projections. narrative extension narrative documents, events, kernel, observations, places, provenance Narrative frames and myth tellings for the deception slice's worked examples and creative works. The narrative interior (#361 arc samples ⊑ Observation over #359 positions, #362 scoped roles, #363 motifs riding the #360 seam) serves the lbox foundation-docs importer (EPIC #358: 16,445 arc samples, 779 role links, 16,002 tags / 669 concepts) ahead of the #364 consumer child. norms extension narrative citations, documents, events, kernel, names, observations, rights, standpoint, teleology, temporal The lbox principia importer (EPIC #348: 4-tier authority hierarchy, special-directive triggers, paradigm precedence) and policy import/export (ODRL round-trip; OPA/Rego, Cedar, XACML down-projection — deferred to the compiler-arc window with the alignment set). The rubrics facility (#353) lives in this slice (Rubric ⊑ Norm; the P16 DAG rule bars extension→extension dependencies): consumers are the lm-eval-harness task projection, the principia RLAIF axes/score-anchor import, and LLM-judge score ingestion as vantage-indexed Assessments. The registers & personas facility (#355) also lives here (expressesNorm → Norm, activatedIn → Condition; same P16 DAG rationale): consumers are system-prompt assembly (Persona × Norms × StyleGuide — the projection that replaces principia.yaml's Jinja2 role, deferred to the compiler-arc window with the alignment set) and the principia persona_modes/paradigm-activation import. notation extension — kernel, language, observations, temporal Symbolic/notation systems for the language family and the music slice's projections (#318). notes extension — evidence, kernel PKM annotations (#63) over core evidence spans; Web Annotation projection. observations core claims, memory entities, events, kernel, names, places, temporal The unified observation stance: every measured, claimed, or sensed value in any slice; the claim layer (#54). organization core — entities, events, kernel, places Employers, publishers, registrars across slices; posts and roles; the W3C-ORG projection. places core memory coreference, documents, kernel, lifecycle, observations, rights, temporal Every located fact: contacts, events, the mail corpus, jurisdiction tenures; the GeoSPARQL projection. procedures extension — events, kernel The universal process/procedure/plan generalization (#226) for workflows and recipes. profiles core — kernel, places, temporal The Profile pattern under every reference frame: temporal, spatial, currency, and tuning frames (#308). provenance core claims, memory documents, events, kernel Every attributed fact (P9): statement-layer attribution, import activities, GTS chain-of-custody. quality core — kernel, observations Data-quality claims (DQV/ISO 19157) over any slice's instance data; the coverage gates. rights core — agreements, kernel, observations, provenance Licensing of every artifact: the ontology's own dual licence, images, software, the mail corpus. risk extension narrative events, kernel The lbox principia importer (EPIC #348: failure_cascades — Trust Collapse and five siblings as named, graded, type-level chains) and threat-model worked examples (D3FEND countermeasures ↔ Mitigation; bowtie barriers ↔ mitigationCounters on CausalLinks). The norms (#351) and procedures extensions plug in through Mitigation's deliberately open measure range — no extension→extension dependency exists or may exist (P16 DAG rule). sensory extension — kernel, observations, places Sensory perception observations (the unified stance applied to senses). sensory-environment extension — kernel, observations, places, temporal Environmental sensing context for sensory observations. sexuality core — entities, gender Identity facets on persons (P16: core by commitment); the 7-axis orthogonality matrix. software extension — attestation, creative-works, entities, events, kernel, language, names, provenance, rights, tags The five-facet software model (#231): git-as-provenance, verifiable releases, this repo itself. sources core claims, memory documents Content-addressed sources under the claim spine and the GTS packages (blake3 digests). standpoint core claims, memory kernel, observations, temporal Every contested fact and every model disagreement (P9); the statement layer; the deception slice. tags core memory kernel, temporal Folksonomy tagging reused by images and software (forced core by dual extension use). teleology core — events, kernel, temporal The agent-memory flagship (an agent recording its own goals across sessions — Principle 14) and the lbox principia importer (EPIC #348: 21-goal hierarchy with counter-goals and tier tenure). The norms extension (#351) ranges prescribedConduct over Goal. temporal core memory kernel, profiles Every slice carrying time-scoped facts (tenures, residences, validity); the statement layer's validFrom/validUntil; the calendar slice; the mail corpus. trust core — accounts, kernel Keys, certifications, and cryptographic signatures used by email wire-auth and attestation. versions core — kernel, observations, temporal Version lineage for software, languages, creative works, and the ontology's own releases.
